# Motion writing format

<!-- Generated by kition-sdk tools/writing-format.mjs from the Motion engine and agent/guide.md. Regenerate it; do not edit it by hand. -->

What a model or a script writes to make or change a Motion document: the run syntax, every
command and its parameters, the value lists and the defaults the engine states, and worked examples.
It is made from the command catalogue of the Motion engine 0.3.25. Read
[`agent/guide.md`](../agent/guide.md) first: it says how to address things, the workflow, and the
pitfalls.

## Syntax

Changes are steps of `motion_run`; each step is one command with its parameters as JSON:

```json
motion_run { "path": "<file>", "steps": [{ "command": "<command id>", "params": { … } }] }
```

A run is one step in the document's history. `motion_commands` finds commands by words; the
lists below are the whole catalogue. A parameter marked required must be given; a parameter left out
takes the engine's default (listed where the engine states one). Commands marked (reads) answer
without changing the document.

## Defaults

Defaults the engine states in its schemas (other defaults are named in the parameter descriptions).

| Command | Parameter | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `file.projectSettings` | `workingGamma` | `2.2` |
| `markers.set` | `new` | `true` |
| `view.panelBackground` | `pick` | `true` |

## Commands

678 commands, by menu.

### File > New

- `file.newProject` (writes): Replaces the open project with a new empty one (or the template set in Settings › Project), discarding unsaved changes. Not undoable; save first. No parameters.
- `project.newFolder` (writes): Creates a folder in the project panel (`name`, inside folder `parent`) and selects it. Returns {item}; move items into it with project item commands.
  - `name` string
  - `parent` integer
- `file.newFromTemplate` (writes): Editor window only: opens the Home screen's Templates tab to start a project from a template. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing. No parameters.

### Help

- `file.openDemoProject` (writes): Replaces the open project with the built-in demo project and opens its main composition at 2.5 s. Discards unsaved changes; returns {comp}. No parameters.
- `help.github` (reads): Opens the project's GitHub page in the browser (emits an open-URL request). Changes nothing. No parameters.
- `help.inAppTutorials` (reads): Editor window only: opens the Home screen's Learn tab. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing. No parameters.
- `help.reportIssue` (reads): Opens the issue tracker page in the browser to give feedback. Changes nothing. No parameters.
- `help.enableLogging` (reads): Turns diagnostic logging to a file on or off (`on`, default toggles). Returns {enabled, path}.
  - `on` boolean
- `help.revealLogFile` (reads): Opens the folder holding the log file in the system file browser. Returns {path, url}. No parameters.
- `help.systemReport` (reads): Answers a system compatibility report (build, processor, memory, GPU, fonts) and shows it in the editor; `quiet` skips the window.
  - `quiet` boolean

### File

- `file.open` (writes): Opens the project file at `path` (.kmotion, or an XML .ecprojx), replacing the open project; returns `savedBy`, the version that saved it. A project from a newer version opens with a warning; a file that is not a project fails.
  - `path` file
- `file.save` (writes): Saves the project to its file, or to `path` when given (the project then continues in that file). Fails when the project has no path yet: use file.saveAs.
  - `path` file
- `file.incrementAndSave` (writes): Saves the project as a new numbered file next to the current one (Intro.aep → Intro 2.aep) and continues in it. Fails if the project was never saved. No parameters.
- `file.revert` (writes): Reloads the project from its saved file, discarding every change since the last save. Fails if the project was never saved. No parameters.
- `file.projectSettings` (writes): Changes project settings: `bitDepth` 8|16|32, colour engine and `workingSpace`, `linearize`, `blendLinear`, HDR handling, `outputSpace`, renderer gpu|software and `timeDisplay` (timecode or frames). Affects every comp's rendering.
  - `bitDepth` integer, one of `8` | `16` | `32`
  - `blendLinear` boolean
  - `colorEngine` string, one of `adobe` | `ocio`
  - `hdr` string, one of `clip` | `compand` | `toneMap`
  - `linearize` boolean
  - `outputSpace` string, one of `srgb` | `rec709` | `rec2020` | `p3` | `rec2100pq` | `rec2100hlg`
  - `renderer` string, one of `gpu` | `software`
  - `timeDisplay` string, timecode|frames|feet35|feet16
  - `workingGamma` number, default `2.2`, with no working space
  - `workingSpace` string, one of `none` | `srgb` | `rec709` | `rec2020` | `p3` | `acescg` | `aces2065`
- `layer.addItem` (writes): Places a project item (`item` id or name: footage, comp or solid) in the active comp as a new layer: starting at `time` (seconds), at stack `index` (1-based, default above the selected layer), at `position` [x, y]; `duration` for stills.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `duration` number, s, for a still
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); 1-based stack position; default above the selected layer
  - `item` integer, id|name
  - `position` number, [x, y] comp px; default the centre
  - `time` number, s, the In point
- `file.close` (writes): File ▸ Close: closes the active composition's tab (or `comp`). The comp stays in the project.
  - `comp` integer or string
- `file.closeProject` (writes): Closes the project and starts an empty one in its place, discarding unsaved changes; save first with the host's save. Not undoable. No parameters.
- `file.newCompFromSelection` (writes): File ▸ New Comp from Selection.
  - `addToRenderQueue` boolean
  - `dimensionsFrom` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `duration` number, s, for stills
  - `overlap` boolean
  - `overlapDuration` number, s
  - `sequence` boolean
  - `single` boolean, one comp for all
  - `transition` string, one of `off` | `dissolveFront` | `crossDissolve`
- `file.reloadFootage` (writes): Reload items `ids`. `undoable` makes it an edit; otherwise it records the disk without modifying the project, and an item whose file can't be read now (another app is still writing it) is left as it was. Returns the number reloaded and the files that couldn't be read (only without `undoable`).
  - `item` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `items` integer[]
- `file.revealInFinder` (writes): Opens the folder holding footage `item`'s file in the system file browser. Returns {url}; fails for items that are not files.
  - `item` integer
  - `items` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `file.watchFolder` (writes): Watches `folder` for .kmotion projects with queued renders, renders them and writes `<project>.status.json` beside each; renders what is there now and returns it. `stop: true` stops watching.
  - `folder` file
  - `path` file, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `stop` boolean
- `app.find` (reads): Editor window only: focuses the project panel search (`query`). Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; use project queries instead.
  - `query` string
- `templates.saveAs` (writes): Saves the current project as a user project template `name` (with `description`, `category`); the active comp becomes its main comp. Footage is embedded up to `embedLimitMB` (256), larger files stay linked.
  - `category` string
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `description` string
  - `embedFootage` boolean, default true: the footage files go into the template
  - `embedLimitMB` number, default 256: footage beyond it stays linked, with a warning
  - `name` string
  - `overwrite` boolean, default true

### File > Save As

- `file.saveAs` (writes): Saves the project to `path` and continues editing that file. Use file.saveCopy to write a copy and keep working in the original.
  - `path` file
- `file.saveCopy` (reads): Writes a copy of the project to `path` and keeps working in the current file. Returns {path, bytes}.
  - `path` file
- `file.saveCopyAsXml` (reads): Writes a copy of the project as XML (.ecprojx) to `path`, for tools that read XML; keeps working in the current file. Returns {path, bytes}.
  - `path` file, .ecprojx

### File > Import

- `file.import` (writes): File ▸ Import; with `addToComp` (files dropped on the Timeline or the Composition viewer) they also become layers of the active comp ([`add_to_comp`]).
  - `addToComp` boolean, also add them to the active comp, at time?, index?, position? as in layer.addItem
  - `alphabetical` boolean, Force Alphabetical Order: every image of that type in the folder, by name
  - `background` boolean, probe the files in a background job, jobs.list / jobs.wait; returns {job}
  - `drag` boolean, dropped files: Settings ▸ Import ▸ Default Drag Import As; files import as stills unless sequence
  - `frameRate` number, fps (image sequences; default Settings ▸ Import ▸ Sequence Footage)
  - `importAs` string, one of `footage` | `composition` | `compositionLayerSizes`, Photoshop, PDF, Illustrator and EPS files
  - `layer` integer, name|index (footage of one Photoshop layer); footage of one Photoshop layer
  - `page` string, number from 1 (PDF / Illustrator page); PDF / Illustrator page
  - `paths` file[], files or folders
  - `sequence` boolean, the Sequence checkbox: true imports numbered stills of one run as one image sequence, one picked file bringing its whole run and several picked files that range; default: a numbered still brings its run, except dropped files (drag), which import as stills as in After Effects; folders' runs import as sequences; false imports stills and a folder's files individually
- `file.importMultiple` (writes): Imports several files at once (`paths`), exactly as file.import with that list: footage, image sequences or projects become project items.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `paths` file[]
- `file.importPlaceholder` (writes): Adds a placeholder footage item (`name`, `width`, `height`, `frameRate`, `duration` seconds) that stands in for media you will replace later. Returns {item}.
  - `duration` number, s
  - `frameRate` number
  - `height` number
  - `name` string
  - `width` number
- `file.importSolid` (writes): Adds a solid footage item (`name`, `color`, `width`, `height`) to the project's Solids folder without placing it in a comp; use layer.newSolid to add a solid layer to a comp. Returns {item}.
  - `color` string
  - `height` number
  - `name` string
  - `width` number
- `file.importLottie` (writes): Imports a Lottie animation from `path` (.json or .lottie) as a new composition of shape, text and image layers, and opens it; embedded images are written beside the file. Returns the comp and warnings.
  - `path` file, .json or .lottie
- `file.importTimeline` (writes): Imports an editing timeline from `path` (Final Cut Pro XML exported from Premiere Pro, .fcpxml, .otio, .edl, .aaf, .omf) as compositions with its clips; `edlFrameRate` for EDLs. Native .prproj is refused.
  - `edlFrameRate` number
  - `format` string, one of `auto` | `xml` | `fcpxml` | `otio` | `edl` | `aaf` | `omf`
  - `path` file, .xml Final Cut Pro XML from Premiere Pro or .fcpxml .otio .edl .aaf .omf
- `file.importVanishingPoint` (writes): Import an exported preset (renamed if the name is taken) and activate it. No parameters.
- `templateProps.importTemplate` (writes): Imports an .ectemplate from `path`: its compositions and media enter the project; `addToComp: true` also places the template's comp as a layer in `comp`. Returns the imported items.
  - `addToComp` boolean
  - `comp` integer
  - `path` file, .ectemplate

### (no menu)

- `file.cycleBitDepth` (writes): Steps the project colour depth 8 → 16 → 32 bits per channel and back. Returns the new label; set a specific depth with file.projectSettings `bitDepth`. No parameters.
- `render.backend` (writes): Video Rendering and Effects: report or set the renderer (Mercury GPU Acceleration when a GPU adapter exists, else Mercury Software Only).
  - `backend` string, one of `gpu` | `cpu`
  - `renderer` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `roto.models` (reads): Lists the Rotoscope Brush models: id, name, whether each is installed, its size and which is selected. No parameters.
- `roto.model.select` (writes): Chooses the segmentation model the Rotoscope Brush uses: `id` classical or mobilesam (must be installed); `wait` returns once it is loaded.
  - `id` string, one of `classical` | `mobilesam`
  - `wait` boolean
- `roto.model.install` (writes): Installs Rotoscope Brush model weights from the file at `path`, verified against the registry's SHA-256 (`id` names them); `wait` blocks until installed.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `path` file, weights file
  - `wait` boolean
- `roto.model.download` (writes): Downloads the official Rotoscope Brush model weights `id` and verifies them (desktop only, uses the system curl); `wait` blocks until done.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `wait` boolean
- `roto.model.remove` (writes): Deletes the installed Rotoscope Brush model `id` from disk; segmentation falls back to the classical model.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `face.models` (reads): Lists the face tracking models: id, name, whether each is installed, its size and which one is selected. Read before face.model.select. No parameters.
- `face.model.select` (writes): Chooses the face tracking model face tracking uses: `id` classical or mediapipe-face (must be installed); `wait` returns only once it is loaded.
  - `id` string, one of `classical` | `mediapipe-face`
  - `wait` boolean
- `face.model.install` (writes): Installs a face tracking model from the model file at `path`, verified against the registry's SHA-256 (`id` names it); `wait` blocks until installed. Use face.model.download to fetch the official one instead.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `path` file, model file
  - `wait` boolean
- `face.model.download` (writes): Downloads the official face tracking model `id` and verifies it (desktop only, uses the system curl); `wait` blocks until done. track.mask's faceOutline and faceDetailed methods need an installed model.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `wait` boolean
- `face.model.remove` (writes): Deletes the installed face tracking model `id` from disk. Face tracking falls back to the classical tracker until another model is selected.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `edit.purge` (writes): Frees caches: `what` all (default), memoryAndDisk, memory, disk, image, 3d or snapshot. Clears rendered layer and footage caches, the disk cache and the viewer snapshot; returns what was freed. The project is unchanged.
  - `what` string, all|memoryAndDisk|memory|disk|3d|image|snapshot
- `cache.diskStats` (reads): Returns the disk cache's state: enabled, folder, entries, cached frames and layers, bytes used and limit, hits, misses, writes and evictions ({enabled:false} when there is none). No parameters.
- `edit.history.list` (reads): Returns the branching undo history: every state with index, id, label, parent, depth, whether it is current or in the future, plus the current index and the number of branches. No parameters.
- `edit.history.goto` (writes): jump to a state by `index` (from `edit.history.list`), `id`, or `steps` along the working line (negative = back, like Undo).
  - `id` integer or string, an id; one of several alternative parameters
  - `index` integer, (from edit.history.list) | id? | steps? (negative = back along the line)
  - `redo` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `steps` json, negative = back along the line; one of several alternative parameters
- `comp.open` (writes): Opens the composition `comp` (id or name) in a viewer tab and makes it the active comp.
  - `comp` integer, id|name
  - `item` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `comp.close` (reads): Closes a composition's viewer tab (`comp`, default the active one). The comp stays in the project.
  - `comp` integer or string
- `comp.workArea` (writes): Sets the work area: `start`/`end` in comp seconds, or `set: begin|end` at the current time; the area stays at least one frame and inside the comp. It bounds previews, renders and comp.trimToWorkArea.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `end` number
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `set` string, one of `begin` | `end`, at CTI
  - `start` number
- `comp.setSwitch` (writes): Sets or toggles a composition switch: `switch` hideShy, motionBlur, frameBlending or draft3d; `value` true/false, omitted to toggle. Returns the new value. The layer switches themselves are set per layer.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `switch` string, one of `hideShy` | `motionBlur` | `frameBlending` | `draft3d`
  - `value` boolean
- `comp.addMarker` (writes): Adds a marker at `time` (comp seconds, default the current time) with `comment` to the selected layers, replacing any marker at that time; layers with locked markers are skipped. For comp-level markers use the markers commands.
  - `comment` string
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `time` number
- `layer.select` (reads): Selects layers in the active comp by id, name or #index (`layers`); `add` adds to the selection, `toggle` flips each. Commands without explicit `layers` act on this selection.
  - `add` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` json[], [id|name|#n]
  - `toggle` boolean
- `layer.selectNext` (reads): Selects the layer below the selected one (or the top layer when none is selected), replacing the selection.
  - `add` boolean
- `layer.selectPrevious` (reads): Selects the layer above the selected one (or the bottom layer when none is selected), replacing the selection.
  - `add` boolean
- `layer.setSwitch` (writes): Sets or toggles a layer switch on `layers`: `switch` video, audio, solo, lock, shy, collapse, quality, fx, frameBlend, motionBlur, adjustment, threeD, guide or preserveTransparency; `value` true/false, omitted to toggle.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `merge` string
  - `quality` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `switch` string, one of `video` | `audio` | `solo` | `lock` | `shy` | `collapse` | `quality` | `fx` | `frameBlend` | `motionBlur` | `adjustment` | `threeD` | `guide` | `preserveTransparency`
  - `value` boolean
- `layer.rename` (writes): Renames `layer` (default the selected one) to `name`. Expressions that refer to the layer by its old name are not updated.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string
- `layer.setComment` (writes): Sets the Comment column text of `layers` (default selected). It is a note only; rendering is unchanged.
  - `comment` string
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.setBlendMode` (writes): Sets the blending mode of `layers` (default selected): `mode` Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Add and so on, or `step` ±1 to cycle. Controls how a layer combines with the layers below.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `mode` string, Normal|Multiply|Screen|…
  - `step` integer, ±1
- `layer.setTrackMatte` (writes): Uses `matte` (a layer, or null to remove) as `layer`'s track matte: `kind` alpha (default), alphaInverted, luma or lumaInverted. The matte layer's video is hidden and it shapes the layer's visibility.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `kind` string, one of `alpha` | `alphaInverted` | `luma` | `lumaInverted`
  - `layer` integer
  - `matte` integer or string, layer|null
- `layer.setParent` (writes): Parents `layers` (default selected) to `parent` (a layer, or null to unparent) so they follow its transform. By default their transforms are compensated so nothing moves now (`compensate: false` to keep raw values). Cycles are refused.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `compensate` boolean
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `parent` integer or string, layer|null
- `layer.timing` (writes): Moves or trims `layers` in time: `op` moveInToTime, moveOutToTime, trimInToTime, trimOutToTime (at the current time), or set `start`, `in`, `out` (seconds), or shift by `delta`. Times snap to frames.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `delta` number
  - `in` number
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `merge` string
  - `op` string, one of `moveInToTime` | `moveOutToTime` | `trimInToTime` | `trimOutToTime`
  - `out` number
  - `start` number
- `layer.slip` (writes): Slip edit: move a layer's source (footage or precomp) under its fixed in and out points, like dragging the source-duration bar in After Effects. `delta` in seconds or `frames`; positive moves the source later. Clamped so the source still covers the in–out span.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `delta` number, (seconds) | frames?
  - `frames` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `merge` string
- `layer.slipBack` (writes): Slip edit: moves the layers' source one frame earlier under their fixed In and Out points, so the same span shows different content. Footage and comp layers only; layers with time remapping are skipped.
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.slipForward` (writes): Slip edit: moves the layers' source one frame later under their fixed In and Out points, so the same span shows different content. Footage and comp layers only; layers with time remapping are skipped.
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.setMask` (writes): Sets a mask's `mode` (Add, Subtract, Intersect…) and `inverted` on `layer`, picking the mask by 1-based index, uid or name (`mask`). Fails when the layer has no masks; add one with layer.addMask.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `inverted` boolean
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer, index|uid|name
  - `mode` string
- `layer.addShapeItem` (writes): Adds an item to a shape layer's contents: `kind` group, rect, ellipse, star, polygon, path, fill, stroke, gradient fill/stroke, trim, repeater, round corners, offset, pucker, twist, zig zag, wiggle or merge; `group` to nest. Returns {uid, path}.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `group` integer, uid|path
  - `kind` string, group|rect|ellipse|star|polygon|path|fill|stroke|gfill|gstroke|trim|repeater|round|offset|pucker|twist|zigzag|wiggle|merge
  - `layer` integer
- `layer.setText` (writes): Edits a text layer: replaces `text` (whole or a character `range`) and sets character and paragraph formatting (`font`, `size`, `fill`, `stroke`, `tracking`, `leading`, `justify`, OpenType features, `box`). Keys the source text when animated.
  - `allCaps` boolean
  - `allSmallCaps` boolean
  - `applyFill` boolean
  - `applyStroke` boolean
  - `baseline` string, one of `normal` | `superscript` | `subscript`
  - `box` json[], [x,y,w,h]|null (layer space); layer space
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `composer` string, one of `everyLine` | `singleLine`
  - `contextualAlternates` boolean
  - `direction` string, one of `ltr` | `rtl`
  - `discretionaryLigatures` boolean, OpenType
  - `fauxBold` boolean
  - `fauxItalic` boolean
  - `figureStyle` string, one of `default` | `lining` | `oldStyle`
  - `figureWidth` string, one of `default` | `proportional` | `tabular`
  - `figures` json
  - `fill` string or array, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1)
  - `font` string
  - `fractions` boolean
  - `hangingPunctuation` boolean
  - `indentFirst` number
  - `indentLeft` number
  - `indentRight` number
  - `justify` string, one of `left` | `center` | `right` | `justifyLeft` | `justifyCenter` | `justifyRight` | `justifyAll`
  - `kerning` string or number, metrics|optical|number
  - `layer` integer
  - `leading` number, px|"auto"
  - `ligatures` boolean
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `ordinals` boolean
  - `range` number[], [start, end]; characters; default all
  - `size` number
  - `smallCaps` boolean
  - `spaceAfter` number
  - `spaceBefore` number
  - `ss01` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 1
  - `ss02` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 2
  - `ss03` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 3
  - `ss04` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 4
  - `ss05` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 5
  - `ss06` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 6
  - `ss07` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 7
  - `ss08` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 8
  - `ss09` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 9
  - `ss10` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 10
  - `ss11` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 11
  - `ss12` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 12
  - `ss13` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 13
  - `ss14` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 14
  - `ss15` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 15
  - `ss16` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 16
  - `ss17` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 17
  - `ss18` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 18
  - `ss19` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 19
  - `ss20` boolean, OpenType stylistic set 20
  - `stroke` string or array, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1)
  - `strokeOverFill` boolean
  - `strokeWidth` number
  - `style` string
  - `stylisticAlternates` boolean
  - `stylisticSets` json[], [1–20]
  - `subscript` boolean
  - `superscript` boolean
  - `swash` boolean
  - `text` string
  - `titling` boolean
  - `tracking` number
  - `variations` object, variable font axes; null resets
  - `vertical` boolean
- `layer.style.add` (writes): Adds a layer style to `layers` (default selected): `style` dropShadow, innerShadow, outerGlow, innerGlow, bevelEmboss, satin, colorOverlay, gradientOverlay or stroke (display names work too). `params` sets its settings in the same step (`{"size": 36, "opacity": 60, "color": "#a5b4fc"}`); a wrong name changes nothing and the error lists the right ones. At 1080p a glow or shadow needs a size of about 30, not the default 5.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object
  - `style` string, one of `dropShadow` | `innerShadow` | `outerGlow` | `innerGlow` | `bevelEmboss` | `satin` | `colorOverlay` | `gradientOverlay` | `stroke`, or display name
- `layer.style.remove` (writes): Removes one layer style from `layer` (default the selected layer): `style` by id (dropShadow, outerGlow…), name or uid, or `layerStyles` for the whole group.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `style` string, id|name|uid|layerStyles
- `layer.style.toggle` (writes): Eye switch of a style (or of the whole Layer Styles group: `style: "layerStyles"`).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `style` string, id|name|uid|layerStyles
  - `value` boolean
- `layer.style.globalLight` (writes): Reads (no values) or sets the comp's global light used by layer styles: `angle` and `altitude` degrees (0–90), keyed at `time` when animated. Returns {angle, altitude}.
  - `altitude` number, deg, 0..90
  - `angle` number, deg
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `time` number, s
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `layer.style.list` (reads): Returns `layer`'s layer styles: the Layer Styles group uid and whether it is on, each style (id, name, uid, enabled), and the styles that can be added.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
- `layer.lightSettings` (writes): Changes a light layer: `name`, `kind` (Parallel, Spot, Point, Ambient, Environment; changing it rebuilds the light), `color`, `intensity`, cone angle and feather, falloff, `castsShadows`, shadow darkness and diffusion, `position`, `poi`.
  - `castsShadows` boolean
  - `color` string
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `coneAngle` number
  - `coneFeather` number
  - `falloff` number
  - `falloffDistance` number
  - `intensity` number
  - `kind` string, one of `Parallel` | `Spot` | `Point` | `Ambient` | `Environment`
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string
  - `poi` number[], [x, y, z]
  - `position` number[], [x, y, z]
  - `radius` number
  - `shadowDarkness` number
  - `shadowDiffusion` number
  - `type` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `view.set3DView` (reads): Switches which view a comp's viewer looks through: activeCamera, default, front, left, top, back, right, bottom or custom1-3. Viewer state only; does not move camera layers.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `view` string, one of `activeCamera` | `default` | `front` | `left` | `top` | `back` | `right` | `bottom` | `custom1` | `custom2` | `custom3`
- `view.set3DViewCamera` (reads): Sets the eye [x,y,z], poi [x,y,z] and zoom of a non-camera 3D view (default, orthographic or custom1-3). For the Active Camera view, edit the camera layer's transform instead.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `poi` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `view` string
  - `zoom` number
- `camera.orbit` (writes): Orbits the active 3D view's camera around its point of interest by `yaw` and `pitch` degrees, keying it at the current time; `merge` makes repeated calls one undo step.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `dx` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `dy` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `camera.pan` (writes): Moves the active 3D view's camera sideways and up by `dx`, `dy` comp pixels (position and point of interest together), keyed at the current time.
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number, comp px
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
- `camera.dolly` (writes): Moves the active 3D view's camera along its view direction by `amount` comp pixels (positive = forward), keying its position at the current time; `merge` folds repeated calls into one undo step.
  - `amount` number, px, + = forward
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
- `view.get3D` (reads): Reports a comp's 3D view state: current view id and label, all view ids, the camera it looks through {eye, forward, zoom, ortho}, the active camera layer {id, name, twoNode} and the light layers. Read-only.
  - `comp` integer
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `layer.newModel` (writes): New 3D model layer from a model footage item (`item`) or a file (`path`, imported first).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); 1-based stack position
  - `item` integer, id or name of a 3D model footage item
  - `name` string
  - `path` file, a .gltf
  - `position` number, [x, y] comp px
  - `time` number, s
- `layer.new3dPrimitive` (writes): Adds a 3D primitive layer: `kind` cube, sphere, plane, torus, cone or cylinder with size options, `position` [x, y, z] and material (`baseColor`, `metallic`, `roughness`, `emissive`, shadows). Switches the comp to Advanced 3D.
  - `acceptsLights` boolean
  - `acceptsShadows` number
  - `baseColor` string or array
  - `castsShadows` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `depth` integer
  - `emissive` string or array
  - `height` number
  - `kind` string, one of `cube` | `sphere` | `plane` | `torus` | `cone` | `cylinder`
  - `metallic` number
  - `name` string
  - `position` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `radius` number
  - `rings` json
  - `roughness` number
  - `segments` number
  - `tubeRadius` json
  - `type` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `width` number
- `layer.newPrimitive` (writes): Adds a 3D primitive layer: `kind` cube, sphere, plane, torus, cone or cylinder with size options, `position` [x, y, z] and material (`baseColor`, `metallic`, `roughness`, `emissive`, shadows). Switches the comp to Advanced 3D.
  - `acceptsLights` boolean
  - `acceptsShadows` number
  - `baseColor` string or array
  - `castsShadows` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `depth` integer
  - `emissive` string or array
  - `height` number
  - `kind` string, one of `cube` | `sphere` | `plane` | `torus` | `cone` | `cylinder`
  - `metallic` number
  - `name` string
  - `position` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `radius` number
  - `rings` json
  - `roughness` number
  - `segments` number
  - `tubeRadius` json
  - `type` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `width` number
- `comp.renderer` (writes): Reads (no arguments) or sets the comp's 3D renderer: `renderer` advanced3d (draws 3D model layers, extrusions) or classic3d. Returns {renderer}.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `renderer` string, one of `advanced3d` | `classic3d`, omit to read
  - `value` string
- `material.set` (writes): Sets material options on 3D `layers` at `time`: `castsShadows` and `acceptsShadows` (off, on, only), `acceptsLights`, reflections, `baseColor`, `metallic`, `roughness`, `emissive`, specular and light transmission. Fails if nothing matched.
  - `acceptsLights` boolean
  - `acceptsShadows` string, one of `off` | `on` | `only`
  - `ambient` number
  - `appearsInReflections` boolean
  - `baseColor` string or array
  - `castsShadows` string, one of `off` | `on` | `only`
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `diffuse` number
  - `emissive` string or array
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `lightTransmission` number
  - `metal` number
  - `metallic` number
  - `roughness` number
  - `specularIntensity` number
  - `specularShininess` number
  - `time` number
- `layer.addTextAnimator` (writes): Adds a text animator with the given `properties` (position, scale, rotation, opacity, fillColor, tracking, blur, characterOffset…) and a range selector to a text layer; animate the selector to reveal per character. `perChar3d` enables 3D.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `enabled` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string
  - `properties` json[], [anchor|position|scale|skew|rotation|opacity|transformAll|lineAnchor|lineSpacing|characterOffset|characterValue|blur|fillColor|fillHue|fillSaturation|fillBrightness|fillOpacity|strokeColor|strokeHue|strokeSaturation|strokeBrightness|strokeOpacity|strokeWidth|tracking|perChar3d]
  - `toggle` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `layer.addTextAnimatorProperty` (writes): Adds `property` (any layer.addTextAnimator property) to an existing text animator (`animator` uid or index) on `layer`, so it is driven by that animator's selectors.
  - `animator` integer, uid|index
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `properties` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `property` json, see layer.addTextAnimator
- `layer.addTextSelector` (writes): Animation ▸ Add Text Selector ▸ Range / Wiggly / Expression (see `layer.addTextSelector`).
  - `animator` integer, uid|index
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `kind` string, one of `range` | `wiggly` | `expression`
  - `layer` integer
- `layer.enablePerChar3D` (writes): Turns per-character 3D on a text layer on (default), off with `enabled: false`, or `toggle`; text animators can then move, rotate and scale each character in 3D. Fails on non-text layers.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `enabled` boolean
  - `layer` integer
  - `toggle` boolean
- `layer.applyTextPreset` (writes): Applies a built-in text animation to a text `layer`: `preset` typewriter, fadeUpCharacters, bounceInWords, trackingIn, scramble, blurIn, jitter or dropInLines, keyed from the current time; or a promo preset from `start` (comp s, default the current time) with timing in frames: blurSlide (per word rise + blur + fade, `variant: subtitle`), letterpress (per character scale + blur), leadWordZoom (first word zoomed and centred, then settles into the line), typewriterFast (0.7 frames per character with a cursor), digitRoll (odometer digits: strip and window layers parented to the text) or countUp (`from`/`to`/`duration`, expo-out, thousands separators). `frames`, `stagger`, `ease`, `by`, `dy`, `blur`, `scale` override the tuned defaults; CJK text goes per character. One undo step; the answer has the animators or layers made and `end`. Fails on non-text layers.
  - `blur` number, pixels; CSS blur radius
  - `by` string, one of `words` | `characters` | `lines`
  - `cursor` string
  - `cycles` integer, extra full turns of a digit roll
  - `decimals` integer
  - `duration` number, seconds
  - `dy` number, pixels
  - `ease` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `frames` number, frames per word, character or digit; typewriterFast: per character
  - `from` number
  - `hold` number, frames the lead word holds
  - `layer` integer or string, a text layer; default the first selected layer
  - `motionBlur` boolean, fast presets turn on layer motion blur, shutter 180, 10 samples; default true
  - `preset` string, one of `typewriter` | `fadeUpCharacters` | `bounceInWords` | `trackingIn` | `scramble` | `blurIn` | `jitter` | `dropInLines` | `blurSlide` | `letterpress` | `leadWordZoom` | `typewriterFast` | `digitRoll` | `countUp`
  - `push` number, fraction the lead word grows over its hold
  - `scale` number, start scale, 1 = 100%
  - `separator` string
  - `stagger` number, frames between units
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time; default the current time
  - `to` number
  - `variant` string, one of `default` | `subtitle`
- `text.presets` (reads): Lists the built-in text animation presets (id, name, description) layer.applyTextPreset accepts, the promo presets included.
  - `description` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `id` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `name` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `text.animatorProperties` (reads): Lists the properties a text animator can drive (position, scale, rotation, opacity, fill and stroke colour, tracking, blur and others) with their labels, for layer.addTextAnimator. No parameters.
- `text.edit` (writes): Starts editing a text layer (the editor's text cursor): selects all text by default, or `select` [anchor, caret], `caret`, or none. Returns {layer, anchor, caret}; typing commands then act there. To set text directly use layer.setText.
  - `caret` integer
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `created` boolean
  - `layer` integer
  - `select` string, [anchor, caret]|"none"
- `text.endEdit` (writes): stop editing (a Type-tool layer left empty is deleted). No parameters.
- `text.fontFeatures` (writes): The OpenType features of a font (`font` / `style`, else the target text layer's style at the caret or its first character), and which Character panel options it sets with its own glyphs (the others are synthesized or have no effect).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `font` string
  - `layer` integer
  - `style` string
- `text.fonts` (reads): The installed font families (bundled and system), with their styles, where each comes from and its name in the font's own language. `query` keeps the families whose English or native name contains it (case-insensitive); `rescan` first looks for fonts installed since the app started.
  - `query` string
  - `rescan` boolean
- `text.setSelection` (writes): Sets the selected character range in the text being edited: `start` and `end` (character indices), or `anchor`/`caret`, or `select: "all"`. Formatting from layer.setText then applies to it.
  - `anchor` json, in one of several forms of the parameters
  - `caret` json, in one of several forms of the parameters
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `end` number, in one of several forms of the parameters
  - `layer` integer, in one of several forms of the parameters
  - `select` string, like all; in one of several forms of the parameters
  - `start` number, in one of several forms of the parameters
- `text.moveCaret` (writes): Moves the text cursor in the text being edited: `to` left, right, wordLeft/Right, lineStart/End, up, down, paraStart/End, start or end; `extend` grows the selection. Needs text.edit first.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `extend` boolean
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `to` string, one of `left` | `right` | `wordLeft` | `wordRight` | `lineStart` | `lineEnd` | `up` | `down` | `paraStart` | `paraEnd` | `start` | `end`
- `text.insert` (writes): Replace the selection (or `range`) with `text`; the caret goes after it.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `range` number[], [start, end]
  - `text` string
- `text.delete` (writes): Delete the selection, or one character / word before (backward) or after the caret.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `direction` string, one of `backward` | `forward`
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `range` number[], [start, end]
  - `word` boolean
- `prop.get` (reads): Reads one property (`layer` plus `path` like transform/position or effects/Glow/radius, or `prop` uid): its value at `time` (comp seconds, default now), type, keyframes with times and interpolation, and expression.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number, comp s
- `prop.set` (writes): Sets a property's value: `path` (e.g. `transform/opacity`, `effects/#1/blurriness`) or `prop` (uid) of `layer`, to `value` (a number, an array, or a colour as "#rrggbb"). On an animated property it adds or changes the keyframe at `time` (layer seconds, or comp seconds with `timeBase: comp`; default the current time). With `selected`, also sets the other selected layers: the same value, or with `offset` the same change from each layer's own value. One undo step (`merge` folds a continuing scrub into one).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `offset` number, them by the same change
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `selected` boolean, also the other selected layers
  - `time` number, layer s by default
  - `timeBase` string, one of `layer` | `comp`
  - `value` number or array or string or object or boolean, the property's value: a number (opacity 0..100, rotation in degrees), a vector [x, y] or [x, y, z], a colour #rrggbb or [r, g, b, a], true or false for a checkbox, text, or an object for shapes and paths
- `prop.toggleAnimation` (writes): Turns animation (the stopwatch) of a property (`path` or `prop` of `layer`) on, keying its current value, or off, removing its keyframes. With `selected`, the other selected layers' same property follows.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `selected` boolean
  - `value` boolean
- `prop.addKey` (writes): Adds a keyframe to one property (`layer` plus `path` such as transform/position, or `prop` uid) at `time` (layer seconds, or comp seconds with `timeBase: comp`; default now), with `value` or the current value. Turns animation on if needed.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number, layer s by default
  - `timeBase` string, one of `layer` | `comp`
  - `value` number or array or string or object or boolean, the property's value: a number (opacity 0..100, rotation in degrees), a vector [x, y] or [x, y, z], a colour #rrggbb or [r, g, b, a], true or false for a checkbox, text, or an object for shapes and paths
- `prop.toggleKey` (writes): Adds a keyframe at the current time to a property (`path` or `prop` of `layer`), or removes the one there. With `selected`, the other selected layers' same property gets (or loses) its keyframe too.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `selected` boolean
- `keys.toggleTransform` (writes): Alt+Shift+A / P / S / R / T: add or remove a keyframe at the current time on that Transform property of every selected layer, in one undo step. Position covers separated X / Y / Z; Rotation on a 3D layer covers Orientation and X / Y / Z Rotation.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `path` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` string, anchor|position|scale|rotation|opacity
  - `time` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `prop.reset` (writes): Resets a property (`path` or `prop`) of `layer`: removes its keyframes and expression; the value becomes `default`, else the property's own default.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `default` json
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `prop.select` (writes): Selects a property (`layer` plus `path` or `prop`); `add` keeps the current selection, `selectKeys` also selects its keyframes. Selecting a mask path selects its points.
  - `add` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `selectKeys` boolean
- `prop.deselect` (writes): Deselect only the named property, preserving unrelated property, layer, key and mask-vertex selections. Selected keys also imply selectedProperties in the script API.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `keys.select` (reads): Selects keyframes: `keys` [{layer, prop uid or path such as transform/position, time}], times in layer seconds unless `timeBase: comp`; `add`/`toggle` extend the selection. Fails on keys that don't exist. Most keys.* commands act on this selection.
  - `add` boolean
  - `keys` object[], [{layer, prop: uid | path (or `path`), time (layer s by default)}]; or `path`; layer s by default
  - `selectProperties` boolean, their properties and layers too, as a Timeline click does
  - `timeBase` string, one of `layer` | `comp`
  - `toggle` boolean, Shift+click: in or out of the selection
- `keys.move` (writes): Shifts the selected keyframes in time by `delta` seconds (negative = earlier), keeping their spacing; `merge` makes repeated calls one undo step. Use keys.nudgeForward/Backward to move by frames.
  - `delta` number, s
  - `merge` string
- `keys.delete` (writes): Deletes the selected keyframes; a property left with no keys keeps the deleted key's value as its static value. Select keys with keys.select first. Returns how many were deleted. No parameters.
- `prop.renameGroup` (writes): Renames a property group (`prop` uid: an effect, mask, shape group or text animator) on `layer` to `name`. Expressions referring to the old name aren't updated.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string
  - `prop` integer, uid
- `prop.setGroupEnabled` (writes): Switches the property group `prop` (uid) on `layer` on or off (`value`): a mask, effect, shape group, text animator or layer style.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `prop` integer, uid
  - `value` boolean
- `prop.removeGroup` (writes): Deletes the property group `prop` (uid) from `layer`, with everything under it: a mask, an effect, a shape group, a text animator or a layer style.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `prop` integer, uid
- `prop.duplicateGroup` (writes): Duplicates the property group `prop` (uid) on `layer` (a mask, effect, shape group or text animator) next to the original; answers the new group's uid.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `prop` integer, uid
- `prop.moveGroup` (writes): Moves a property group (`prop` uid: an effect, mask, shape item or text animator) to position `index` (1-based) among its siblings, e.g. to change effect or shape stacking order.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); 1-based among its siblings
  - `layer` integer
  - `prop` integer, uid
- `project.select` (reads): Selects project items by id or name (`items`); `add` adds to the selection. Returns the selected ids; item commands without `items` act on it.
  - `add` boolean
  - `items` json[], [id|name]
- `project.rename` (writes): Renames a project item (`item` id or name, default the selected one) to `name`. Layer names using it are unchanged.
  - `item` integer, id|name (default: selected); default: selected
  - `name` string
- `project.move` (writes): Move items into `folder` (id/name; `null` = the project root).
  - `folder` integer or string, id|name|null (root)
  - `item` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `items` json[], [id|name] (default: selected); default: selected
- `project.setLabel` (writes): Sets the label colour of project `items` (default selected): `label` a colour name or index 0–16.
  - `item` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `items` integer[]
  - `label` string, name|index
- `project.setComment` (writes): Sets the Comment column text of project `items` (default selected). A note only.
  - `comment` string
  - `item` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `items` integer[]
- `project.delete` (writes): Delete project items (folders with their contents). Layers that use a deleted item and Render Queue items of deleted comps go too, like After Effects' Edit ▸ Clear in the Project panel.
  - `items` json[], [id|name] (default: selected); default: selected
- `project.usage` (reads): Returns what deleting `items` (default selected) would remove: the item count including folder contents, and the layers and compositions that use them. Changes nothing.
  - `item` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `items` json[], [id|name] (default: selected); default: selected
- `project.duplicate` (writes): Duplicate project items (Edit ▸ Duplicate in the Project panel): comps get fresh layer ids and a numbered name; the copies are selected.
  - `items` json[], [id|name] (default: selected); default: selected
- `keys.copy` (writes): Copy the selected keyframes (Edit ▸ Copy with keys selected). No parameters.
- `keys.paste` (writes): Paste copied keyframes at the current time into the target layers' properties.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number
- `keys.selectAll` (reads): Select every keyframe of the selected properties, or of the given / selected layers.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `prop` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `visible` object[], [{layer, prop}] (every key of these properties); every key of these properties
- `keys.nudge` (writes): Move the selected keys by whole frames (Alt+→ / Alt+←, Shift for 10 frames).
  - `frames` integer
  - `merge` string
- `keys.nudgeForward` (writes): Moves the selected keyframes one frame later. keys.move shifts by any number of seconds.
  - `frames` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `keys.nudgeBackward` (writes): Moves the selected keyframes one frame earlier. keys.move shifts by any number of seconds.
  - `frames` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `keys.nudgeForward10` (writes): Moves the selected keyframes ten frames later.
  - `frames` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `keys.nudgeBackward10` (writes): Moves the selected keyframes ten frames earlier.
  - `frames` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `keys.set` (writes): Edit one key directly: move it in time and/or set its value (Graph Editor drags).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `newTime` json, same base
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number, layer s by default
  - `timeBase` string, one of `layer` | `comp`
  - `value` number or array or string or object or boolean, the property's value: a number (opacity 0..100, rotation in degrees), a vector [x, y] or [x, y, z], a colour #rrggbb or [r, g, b, a], true or false for a checkbox, text, or an object for shapes and paths
- `keys.selectEqual` (writes): Adds to the selection every keyframe, on the same properties, whose value equals a selected keyframe's value. No parameters.
- `keys.selectPrevious` (writes): Adds to the selection every keyframe before the first selected one on the same properties. No parameters.
- `keys.selectFollowing` (writes): Adds to the selection every keyframe after the last selected one on the same properties. No parameters.
- `keys.setEase` (writes): Set one side's temporal ease of a key (Graph Editor handle drags, scripting).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `dim` integer
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `side` string, one of `in` | `out`
  - `speed` number
  - `time` number, layer s
- `keys.info` (reads): Returns details of the selected keyframes, or `keys` [{layer, prop, time}]: value, interpolation in and out, ease speed and influence per side and dimension, spatial tangents and roving, with units.
  - `keys` object[], [{layer, prop, time}]
- `keys.wiggle` (writes): Wiggler: adds random keyframes between two selected keys on a property: `frequency` keys per second (5), `magnitude` in property units, `noise` smooth or jagged, `dimensions` one/same/independent, `seed` for repeatability.
  - `apply` string, one of `spatial` | `temporal`
  - `dimension` integer, index for `one`
  - `dimensions` string, one of `one` | `same` | `independent`
  - `frequency` number, keys/s, 5
  - `magnitude` number
  - `noise` string, one of `smooth` | `jagged`
  - `quality` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `seed` integer
  - `tolerance` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `keys.smooth` (writes): Smoother: removes keyframes from the selected run (three or more keys on a property) where the curve stays within `tolerance` of the original (property units, default 1), simplifying hand-drawn or tracked motion.
  - `tolerance` number, property units, 1
- `motion.sketch` (writes): Motion Sketch: `points` are `[t, x, y]` (t = capture seconds from the start) or `[x, y]` (one per frame); recorded from `start` (default the current time).
  - `captureSpeed` number, %, 100
  - `layer` integer
  - `points` json[], [[t, x, y]…] (t = capture seconds) | [[x, y]…] (one per frame); t = capture seconds; one per frame
  - `smoothing` number, px, 1
  - `start` number, s, default current time
- `prop.pickWhip` (writes): Links one property to another with an expression, as the pick whip does: `target` {layer, path or prop, dimension} sets e.g. thisComp.layer("A").transform.position[0]; `expression` with `range` inserts the reference into existing text.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `expression` string
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `range` number[], [start, end]
  - `target` object, {layer, path|prop, dimension?}
- `markers.list` (reads): Lists markers: the comp's markers, or `layer`'s (layer markers): index, time, duration, comment, chapter, URL, cue point and label, with times in comp seconds.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, omit for composition markers
- `markers.nested` (reads): Lists the markers of a precomp `layer`'s nested composition at the times they fall in this comp, as the layer bar shows them: time, nested time, duration, comment and label.
  - `comp` integer
  - `layer` integer, a precomp layer
- `markers.set` (writes): Edit (or with `new: true`, add) a marker. Returns its new index.
  - `at` json, comp s; one of several alternative parameters
  - `chapter` string
  - `comment` string
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `cuePoint` string, {name, navigation?, params?: [[name, value]…]} | null
  - `duration` number, s
  - `frameTarget` string
  - `index` integer, (0-based) | at? (comp s) | new?: true
  - `kind` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `label` string
  - `layer` integer, omit: comp marker
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `name` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `new` boolean, default `true`, one of several alternative parameters
  - `protected` boolean
  - `time` number, comp s
  - `url` string
- `markers.delete` (writes): Deletes a marker: by `index` (from 0) or the one at `at` (comp seconds), of `layer`, or of the comp when no `layer` is given.
  - `at` number, comp s; one of several alternative parameters
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); comp s; one of several alternative parameters
  - `layer` integer
- `markers.convert` (writes): Layer marker → comp marker (when `layer` is given), or comp marker → layer marker on `toLayer` (default: the selected layers).
  - `at` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `layer` integer, layer marker → comp marker
  - `toLayer` json, comp marker → layer marker
- `mask.new` (writes): Pen tool: a new (open by default) mask from points.
  - `closed` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `inTangents` array[], [[x, y], …]
  - `layer` integer
  - `mode` string
  - `outTangents` array[], [[x, y], …]
  - `vertices` array
- `mask.addVertex` (writes): Adds a vertex at `point` [x, y] (layer pixels) to `mask` on `layer`, at `index` (default the end), with optional tangents `in`/`out`. Returns the new vertex index and selects it.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `in` number
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `out` number
  - `point` number[]
- `mask.setVertex` (writes): Moves one vertex (`index`) of `mask` to `point` [x, y] and/or sets its `in`/`out` tangents (layer pixels, relative to the vertex), at the current time. Fails on an index the path doesn't have.
  - `in` number
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `out` number
  - `point` json
- `mask.selectVertices` (reads): Selects mask vertices `vertices` [{layer, mask, index}]; `add` adds them, with `toggle` flipping those already selected. Returns the selection count; mask.moveVertices and mask.deleteVertices act on it.
  - `add` boolean
  - `toggle` boolean
  - `vertices` object[], [{layer, mask, index}]
- `mask.moveVertices` (writes): Moves the selected mask vertices, or `vertices` [{layer, mask, index}], by `delta` [dx, dy] in layer pixels at the current time (keyed when the path is animated); `merge` makes repeated calls one undo step.
  - `delta` number[], [dx, dy]
  - `index` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `mask` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `merge` string
  - `vertices` object[], [{layer, mask, index}]
- `mask.deleteVertices` (writes): Deletes the selected mask vertices, or `vertices`; a path left with fewer than three vertices becomes open. Returns how many were deleted.
  - `index` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `mask` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `vertices` json
- `mask.convertVertex` (writes): Convert Vertex tool: a corner vertex becomes smooth (tangents along its neighbours, a sixth of their distance each way), a smooth one becomes a corner (no tangents). `smooth` forces one.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer, uid (mask or shape Path item); mask or shape Path item
  - `smooth` boolean
  - `tolerance` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `mask.insertVertex` (writes): Add Vertex tool: insert a vertex on segment `segment` at parameter `t` (default 0.5).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer, uid (mask or shape Path item); mask or shape Path item
  - `segment` integer
  - `t` number, 0 to 1
- `mask.featherPoint.add` (writes): Mask Feather tool: add a feather point on the path, by `segment`/`t` or at the path position nearest `point` (layer space). Without `radius`, a `point` off the path sets it from its distance (outside the mask = outer feather, inside = inner).
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `point` number[], layer space
  - `radius` number, px, negative = inner
  - `segment` integer
  - `t` number, 0 to 1
  - `tension` number, %
- `mask.featherPoint.set` (writes): Drag a feather point: move it along the path (`segment`/`t`, or nearest `point`) and/or set its `radius` (signed: negative = inner) and `tension` (%).
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `point` json, slide along the path
  - `radius` number
  - `segment` integer
  - `t` number
  - `tension` number, %
  - `toward` number[], radius from the drag point, layer space
- `mask.featherPoint.remove` (writes): Deletes a variable-width feather point (`index`) from `mask`, or all of them with `all: true`. Returns how many remain.
  - `all` boolean, one of several alternative parameters
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
- `mask.featherPoint.list` (reads): Lists the variable-width feather points on `mask` at the current time: segment, position along it (t), radius and tension.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
- `mask.remove` (writes): Deletes `mask` (uid, name or index) from `layer` (default the selected layer). layer.mask.remove works on the selected masks.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
- `mask.removeAll` (writes): Deletes every mask on `layer` (default the selected layer).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `layer.mask.motionBlur` (writes): Sets a mask's motion blur: `mode` sameAsLayer (follows the layer's switch), on or off.
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `mode` string, one of `sameAsLayer` | `on` | `off`
- `layer.mask.featherFalloff` (writes): Sets how a mask's feather fades: `mode` smooth or linear, for `mask` (default selected masks) on `layer`.
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `mode` string, one of `smooth` | `linear`
  - `tolerance` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `effect.apply` (writes): Applies an effect (`effect`: id or name, e.g. "Gaussian Blur", "Gradient Ramp", "Glow") to `layers` (default selected). `params` sets its settings in the same step, by name or match id (`{"Blurriness": 30}`, `{"Start Color": "#1d4ed8"}`); a wrong name changes nothing and the error lists the right ones. Answers each instance's path (`effects/#2`) and the parameters with their paths and values, to change or animate with prop.set and prop.addKey.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` string, id|name (e.g. Gaussian Blur); e.g. Gaussian Blur
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object
- `layer.channels` (reads): Returns the layers and channels of a multi-layer OpenEXR footage `layer` and what each EXR layer maps to red, green, blue and alpha; these are the names EXtractoR's channel parameters take. Empty for other layers.
  - `channel` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `colorized` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `toggle` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `effect.pickColor` (writes): A colour parameter's eyedropper on a keyer (Effect Controls): the colour of the effect's input (the layer's pixels before this effect, so a keyed screen can still be picked) at a layer-space point, set on the parameter. `average` takes the 5 × 5 pixels around it.
  - `average` boolean, 5×5
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string, index|uid|name
  - `layer` integer
  - `param` string, id (e.g. screenColour) | prop: uid; e.g. screenColour
  - `prop` json, uid; one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number, effect space
- `effect.remove` (writes): Removes the effect `effect` (index from 1, uid or name) from `layer` (default the selected layer).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string, index|uid|name
  - `effects` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
- `effect.toggle` (writes): Switches the effect `effect` on `layer` on or off (`value`; without it, toggles). A switched-off effect does not render.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
  - `value` boolean
- `effect.reorder` (writes): Moves one effect (`effect` by uid, name or index) on `layer` to position `index` (1-based) in the effect stack; effects render top to bottom, so order changes the result.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `layer` integer
- `effect.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates the effect `effect` (index from 1, uid or name) on `layer`, below the original, with its settings and keyframes.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
- `effect.copy` (writes): Edit ▸ Copy with effects selected: puts the effect instances on the effect clipboard.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` json[], [uid|name|index]; one of several alternative parameters
  - `effects` json[], [uid|name|index]; one of several alternative parameters
  - `layer` integer
- `effect.paste` (writes): Edit ▸ Paste with effects on the clipboard: adds copies to every target layer, after the layer's selected effect when it has one, else at the end of its stack.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `effect.reset` (writes): Effect Controls' Reset: every parameter back to its default. Animated parameters get a keyframe at the current time with the default value (as in After Effects); static ones change their value.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
- `effect.list` (reads): Lists the effects effect.apply accepts (`filter` matches names or ids) with each parameter's id, name, type, default, popup options, ranges and decimals; popup values are zero-based. Point defaults are in pixels of a comp-sized layer of the active comp (`unit` px, as prop.set takes them), or fractions of the layer size when no comp is open (`unit` layer). Read before effect.apply or setting effect properties.
  - `filter` string
- `effect.warning` (reads): Returns what Effect Controls warns about one effect (`effect` by index, uid or name, default the selected one) at `time`: e.g. an unreadable OCIO config or transforms it passes through; `warning` is null when it renders as asked.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string, index|uid|name (default: the selected effect)
  - `layer` integer
  - `time` number
- `effect.plugins.list` (reads): Lists the registered plug-in effects (WebAssembly or Rust): id, name, category, version, author, description, source and parameter ids, plus the plug-in API version and whether WebAssembly plug-ins can load.
  - `filter` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `effect.plugins.load` (writes): load WebAssembly effect plug-ins (a file, or every `.wasm` in a folder) through the host's loader ([`Session::plugin_loader`]).
  - `filter` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `folder` file, loads every .wasm in it; one of several alternative parameters
  - `path` file, .wasm / .wat plug-in, API v1; one of several alternative parameters
- `time.nextFrame` (reads): Moves the current time one frame later.
  - `frames` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `time.previousFrame` (reads): Moves the current time one frame earlier.
  - `frames` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `time.forward10` (reads): Moves the current time 10 frames later.
  - `frames` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `time.back10` (reads): Moves the current time 10 frames earlier.
  - `frames` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `time.step` (reads): Moves the current time by `frames` (negative = earlier). Returns the new time; most commands without an explicit time act at the current time.
  - `frames` integer
- `time.start` (reads): Moves the current time to the first frame of the composition.
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `to` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `visible` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `time.end` (reads): Moves the current time to the last frame of the composition.
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `to` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `visible` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `time.layerIn` (reads): Moves the current time to the selected layer's In point.
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `to` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `visible` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `time.layerOut` (reads): Moves the current time to the selected layer's last frame (its Out point).
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `to` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `visible` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `time.nextKey` (reads): Moves the current time to the next keyframe or marker visible in the timeline.
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `to` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `visible` object[], [{layer, prop}] (only these properties' keys, as the Timeline shows them); only these properties' keys, as the Timeline shows them
- `time.previousKey` (reads): Moves the current time to the previous keyframe or marker visible in the timeline.
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `to` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `visible` object[], [{layer, prop}]
- `time.go` (reads): Moves the current time `to` start, end, workStart, workEnd, layerIn/layerOut (the selected layer), or nextKey/prevKey (keyframes of `prop` or the visible properties, markers and the work area).
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` integer, uid
  - `to` string, one of `start` | `end` | `workStart` | `workEnd` | `layerIn` | `layerOut` | `nextKey` | `prevKey`
  - `visible` object[], [{layer, prop}]
- `renderQueue.remove` (writes): Removes an item from the render queue: `item` (id) or `index`.
  - `index` integer
  - `item` integer, an id
- `renderQueue.setRender` (writes): Ticks or unticks an item's Render checkbox (`render`, default toggles): only ticked (queued) items render. Returns {render}.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `render` boolean, toggles
  - `wait` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `renderQueue.setRenderSettings` (writes): Changes a Render Queue item's render settings: `quality`, `resolution`, proxies, effects and solo overrides, `colorDepth`, frame blending, motion blur, `timeSpan` (workArea, comp or custom with `start`/`end` seconds), `frameRate`, or a `template`.
  - `colorDepth` string, one of `current` | `8` | `16` | `32`, current|8|16|32
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `duration` number, s
  - `effects` string, one of `current` | `allOn` | `allOff`
  - `end` number, s
  - `fieldRender` string, one of `off` | `upper` | `lower`
  - `frameBlending` string, one of `current` | `onForChecked` | `offForAll`
  - `frameRate` json, fps|null
  - `guideLayers` string, one of `current` | `allOff`
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `motionBlur` boolean, bool|current|onForChecked|offForAll
  - `proxyUse` string, one of `current` | `all` | `comp` | `none`
  - `pulldown` string, one of `off` | `WSSWW` | `SSWWW` | `SWWWS` | `WWWSS` | `WWSSW`
  - `quality` string, one of `best` | `draft`
  - `resolution` number, full|half|third|quarter|scale
  - `skipExisting` boolean
  - `solo` string, one of `current` | `allOff`
  - `start` number, s
  - `storageOverflow` boolean
  - `template` string
  - `timeSpan` string, one of `workArea` | `comp` | `custom`
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `renderQueue.setOutputModule` (writes): Changes a Render Queue item's output module: `format` (h264, hevc, av1, prores, webm, image sequences, gif, audio), channels and alpha, quality or bitrate, codec profile, crop, resize, audio settings and post-render action, or a `template`.
  - `audio` string, one of `auto` | `on` | `off`
  - `audioBitrate` number, Opus kbps
  - `audioChannels` string, one of `mono` | `stereo`
  - `audioFormat` integer, one of `16` | `24` | `32`
  - `bitrate` number, kbps
  - `channels` string, one of `rgb` | `rgba` | `alpha`
  - `color` string, one of `straight` | `premultiplied`
  - `crop` boolean, bool|{useRoi?
  - `cropBottom` json
  - `cropLeft` json
  - `cropRight` json
  - `cropTop` json
  - `format` string, one of `h264` | `hevc` | `av1` | `prores` | `webm` | `png` | `jpeg` | `tiff` | `exr` | `gif` | `wav` | `aiff`
  - `includeProjectLink` boolean
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `keyframeInterval` integer, frames; 0 = auto
  - `level` number, auto|4.1
  - `loop` boolean
  - `module` integer, 1 = first
  - `opusApplication` string, one of `audio` | `voice`
  - `output` string
  - `postRenderAction` string, one of `none` | `import` | `importAndReplace` | `setProxy`
  - `profile` string, one of `main` | `main10`, HEVC/AV1
  - `proresProfile` string, proxy|lt|standard|hq|4444|4444xq
  - `quality` integer, 1-100
