  - `rateControl` string, one of `bitrate` | `quality`
  - `resize` object, bool|{preset?, width?, height?, lockAspect?, quality?: low|high}
  - `resizeHeight` json
  - `resizeWidth` json
  - `sampleRate` integer
  - `template` string
  - `webmBitrate` boolean
  - `webmCodec` string, one of `vp9` | `av1`
- `renderQueue.setOutput` (writes): Sets where a Render Queue item's output module (`module`, default the first) writes: `path` a file path or a template such as [compName].[fileExtension]. Re-queues a finished item. Returns the item.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `module` integer
  - `output` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `path` file, file path or template like [compName].[fileExtension]
- `renderQueue.move` (writes): Moves a Render Queue item (`item` or `index`) to position `to` (1-based); items render in queue order.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `to` integer, 1-based
- `renderQueue.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates a render queue item (`item` id or `index`) with its render settings and output module.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
- `renderQueue.render` (writes): Render a comp frame with the session's footage + expression hosts.
  - `wait` boolean, default true; the UI renders in the background
- `renderQueue.stop` (writes): Stops the render in progress; finished items keep their output. Returns {stopped}. No parameters.
- `renderQueue.list` (reads): Returns the Render Queue: each item's index, comp, status, render checkbox, settings, output modules and paths, plus whether rendering is running and its progress. No parameters.
- `renderQueue.templates` (reads): Lists the render settings and output module templates with their settings and which ones are the defaults per slot. No parameters.
- `renderQueue.saveTemplate` (writes): Save a template: from an item's settings (`item`/`index`, `module`), or the slot default, adjusted by `params` (the same keys as setRenderSettings / setOutputModule).
  - `from` string, template to copy
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); save from this item; one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, save from this item; one of several alternative parameters
  - `kind` string, one of `renderSettings` | `outputModule`
  - `module` integer
  - `name` string
  - `params` object
- `renderQueue.deleteTemplate` (writes): Deletes a render settings or output module template (`kind`, `name`) from the project's templates.
  - `kind` string, one of `renderSettings` | `outputModule`
  - `name` string
- `renderQueue.setTemplateDefault` (writes): Makes template `name` the default for a `slot` (movie, still, preRender, movieProxy, stillProxy) of `kind` renderSettings or outputModule; new queue items use it.
  - `kind` string, one of `renderSettings` | `outputModule`
  - `name` string
  - `slot` string, one of `movie` | `still` | `preRender` | `movieProxy` | `stillProxy`
- `renderQueue.applyTemplate` (writes): Apply templates to an item: `renderSettings` and/or `outputModule` (to `module`).
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `module` integer
  - `outputModule` string, template name
  - `renderSettings` string, template name
- `renderQueue.setLog` (writes): Sets a Render Queue item's log level: `log` errorsOnly, plusSettings or plusPerFrameInfo. Returns the item.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `log` string, one of `errorsOnly` | `plusSettings` | `plusPerFrameInfo`
- `renderQueue.setNotify` (writes): Turns the notification when the queue finishes on or off (`notify`, default toggles).
  - `notify` boolean, toggles
  - `value` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `renderQueue.setOverflowFolders` (writes): Sets the folders used in order when the output volume is full (`folders`, an empty list turns overflow off).
  - `folders` file[], used in order when the output volume is full
- `renderQueue.formats` (reads): Lists the output formats with id, label, extension and whether each is a sequence, supports alpha and audio, and is available in this build, plus the video codec profiles and levels. No parameters.
- `help.docs` (reads): Help ▸ Kition Motion Help / Expression Reference / Effect Reference.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `enabled` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `page` string, one of `help` | `expressions` | `effects`
- `command.list` (reads): Lists the engine's commands with id, label and menu path; `filter` matches ids and labels, `enabledOnly` drops disabled ones, `schemas: true` adds each parameter JSON Schema. Agents usually use <prefix>_commands instead.
  - `enabledOnly` boolean
  - `filter` string
  - `schemas` boolean, add each command's params JSON Schema
- `command.describe` (reads): Returns one command in full: id, label, menu path, shortcut, parameter notes, the JSON Schema of its parameters, whether it is undoable, and whether it is enabled now (with the reason when not).
  - `command` string
  - `id` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `app.capabilities` (reads): Returns what this build can do: version, command count, effect counts (total, GPU, float), export formats, whether import, expressions, scripting and GPU are available, and the After Effects parity summary. No parameters.
- `project.summary` (reads): Returns every project item: id, name, type (composition, footage, solid, folder), label, parent folder, size, duration, and for comps their layer count and frame rate. Start here to find comp and item ids. No parameters.
- `comp.info` (reads): Returns a composition's settings and layers: id, name, size, frame rate, duration (seconds), work area, background, preserve flags, and each layer's index, name, type, in/out points and switches. `comp` defaults to the active one.
  - `comp` integer
- `layer.tree` (reads): Returns `layer`'s property tree at `time` (comp seconds): every group and property with its path (as prop.set takes, e.g. transform/position), value, keyframes and expression, `depth` levels deep. Read before setting properties.
  - `comp` integer
  - `depth` integer
  - `layer` integer
  - `time` number, comp s
- `editor.state` (reads): Returns the editor's session state: active comp, current time, selected layers, properties, keyframes and mask vertices, open panels and viewer settings. Use it to see what selection-based commands will act on. No parameters.
- `engine.batch` (reads): Runs several commands in one call and one undo step: `steps` [{command, params}]; a string "$N" or "$N.key" in params is step N's result (1-based), e.g. {"layer": "$1.layer"}. `atomic` (default true) rolls all back if a step fails.
  - `atomic` boolean, default true: a failing step rolls the whole batch back
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `label` string, undo step name, default Batch
  - `steps` object[], [{command, params?}]
- `layer.quality` (writes): Sets render quality of `layers` (default selected): `quality` best (default), draft (faster, lower quality) or wireframe (outlines only).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `quality` string, one of `best` | `draft` | `wireframe`
- `layer.sampling` (writes): Sets how `layers` (default selected) are resampled when transformed: `sampling` bilinear (default) or bicubic (sharper when scaled).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `sampling` string, one of `bilinear` | `bicubic`
- `layer.frameBlending` (writes): Sets frame blending on `layers` (default selected): `mode` off, frameMix (cross-fades frames) or pixelMotion (motion-interpolated); smooths slowed or time-remapped footage. The comp's frame blending switch must be on to render it.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `mode` string, one of `off` | `frameMix` | `pixelMotion`
- `layer.expressions` (writes): Enables or disables (`enabled`) every expression on `layers` (default selected) without deleting them; disabled expressions keep their text and the property uses its own value. Returns how many changed.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `enabled` boolean
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.setTransform` (writes): Sets a transform property of `layers` at the current time: `prop` anchor, position, scale, orientation, rotation or opacity, `value` a number or [x, y(, z)]. Keys it if animated. For any property path use prop.set.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` string, anchor|position|scale|orientation|rotation|opacity
  - `value` number or array or string or object or boolean, the property's value: a number (opacity 0..100, rotation in degrees), a vector [x, y] or [x, y, z], a colour #rrggbb or [r, g, b, a], true or false for a checkbox, text, or an object for shapes and paths
- `layer.mask.set` (writes): Sets a mask property at the current time: `field` feather (pixels, one number or [x, y]), opacity (%) or expansion (pixels), `value`. Keys it if the property is animated.
  - `field` string, one of `feather` | `opacity` | `expansion`
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `value` string
- `layer.mask.mode` (writes): Sets how a mask combines with the masks above it: `mode` None, Add, Subtract, Intersect, Lighten, Darken or Difference, for `mask` (default selected) on `layer`.
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `mode` string, one of `None` | `Add` | `Subtract` | `Intersect` | `Lighten` | `Darken` | `Difference`
- `layer.trackMatte` (writes): Sets `layers`' track matte in one step: `op` alpha, alphaInverted, luma or lumaInverted uses the layer above as the matte; above or below picks that layer; none removes it.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `op` string, one of `none` | `alpha` | `alphaInverted` | `luma` | `lumaInverted` | `above` | `below`
- `layer.create` (writes): Converts the selected layer by `op`: editableText (Photoshop type layer to a text layer), shapesFromText (a shape layer of the glyph outlines), masksFromText (masks on a solid) or shapesFromVector (SVG/vector footage to a shape layer).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `op` string, one of `editableText` | `shapesFromText` | `masksFromText` | `shapesFromVector`
- `text.addSelector` (writes): Animation ▸ Add Text Selector ▸ Range / Wiggly / Expression (see `layer.addTextSelector`).
  - `animator` integer, uid|index
  - `kind` string, one of `range` | `wiggly` | `expression`
  - `layer` integer
- `anim.reveal` (reads): Reveals (twirls open) properties on the selected layers, or all layers: `kind` keyframes (animated), animation (keys or expressions) or modified (changed from defaults). Returns the revealed property ids; changes no values.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `kind` string, one of `keyframes` | `animation` | `modified`
- `view.layout` (reads): Sets how many viewer panes are shown: `views` 1, 2 or 4. Viewer state only. Returns {views}.
  - `views` integer, one of `1` | `2` | `4`
- `view.extendedViewer` (reads): Settings ▸ 3D ▸ Extended Viewer: 3D views (custom views, or Draft 3D) show the pasteboard around the comp frame with the layers that reach onto it.
  - `value` boolean
- `view.setRegionOfInterest` (reads): Limits viewer previews to `rect` [x, y, w, h] in comp pixels (width and height positive); pass null or omit it to clear. Renders are unaffected. Returns the rect or null.
  - `rect` json[], [x, y, w, h] | null
- `view.snappingOptions` (reads): Tools bar ▸ Snapping options: sets the options passed (`toggle` flips one by key).
  - `collapsedFeatures` json, (Snap to Features in Collapsed Compositions and Text Layers): bool
  - `edgesExtended` json, Snap Edges Extended
  - `toggle` string, one of those keys
- `view.simulateOutput` (reads): View ▸ Simulate Output ▸ (profile). `custom` uses (and with `space` sets) the Custom profile.
  - `preserveRgb` boolean
  - `profile` string, one of `none` | `rec709` | `ntsc` | `pal` | `mac18` | `srgb` | `rec2020` | `p3` | `linear` | `myCustom` | `custom`
  - `space` string, custom
- `view.customRgb` (reads): View ▸ Simulate Output ▸ My Custom RGB…: define the custom output device (kept in Settings) and, unless `apply` is false, simulate it.
  - `apply` boolean, default true: simulate it
  - `from` string, a Simulate Output profile to start from
  - `gamma` number
  - `icc` string, RGB ICC profile, matrix/TRC or LUT-based A2B0: read when it changes, "" clears; a LUT profile simulates through its tables, `lutProfile` in the reply; typed-in numbers replace it
  - `name` string
  - `preserveRgb` boolean
  - `reload` boolean
  - `reset` boolean
  - `srgbCurve` boolean
- `view.closeLockedViewer` (reads): Closes the locked composition viewer, if one is open. Returns {closed}; changes no project content. No parameters.
- `view.displayColor` (reads): Reports the viewer's colour pipeline: displayColorManagement, output simulation {profile, preserveRgb}, customRgb, display profile, project workingSpace, whether display colour is active, and the locked viewer. Read-only. No parameters.
- `view.channel` (reads): Shows one channel in the viewer: `channel` rgb, red, green, blue, alpha or rgbStraight, `colorized` tints single channels, `toggle` returns to RGB when it is already shown. View state only.
  - `channel` string, one of `rgb` | `red` | `green` | `blue` | `alpha` | `rgbStraight`
  - `colorized` boolean
  - `toggle` boolean
- `view.exposure` (reads): Sets the viewer's preview exposure in stops, either absolute (`stops`) or relative (`delta`), clamped to ±40. Affects only the viewer, not renders; view.resetExposure returns it to 0. Returns the new value.
  - `delta` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `stops` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `view.resetExposure` (reads): Sets the viewer's preview exposure back to 0 stops. Returns 0. No parameters.
- `view.takeSnapshot` (reads): Renders the active comp at its current time (with `scale` 0.05-1, default 1) and keeps it as the viewer snapshot for view.showSnapshot. Returns {width, height, time in seconds}.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `scale` number, 0.05 to 1
- `view.showSnapshot` (reads): Sets (`value`) or toggles showing the last viewer snapshot instead of the live frame. Viewer state only. Returns the new value.
  - `value` boolean
- `view.fastPreviewMode` (reads): Sets the viewer's Fast Previews mode: off, adaptive, draft, fastDraft or wireframe. Viewer state only; renders are unaffected. Returns the mode id.
  - `mode` string, one of `off` | `adaptive` | `draft` | `fastDraft` | `wireframe`
- `view.moveGuide` (writes): Moves the guide at `index` (from the comp's guides list) to `position` in comp pixels along its axis. Undoable; `merge` folds repeated moves into one undo step. Returns the position.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `merge` string
  - `position` number, comp px
- `view.removeGuide` (writes): Deletes the guide at `index` from the comp's guides list. Undoable. Indices of later guides shift down by one.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `shape.newPath` (writes): Pen tool on a shape layer: a new Shape group ("Shape n" with Path 1 and the Tools bar's Stroke and Fill unless given) on the given / selected shape layer, or on a new shape layer when none is given. Vertices are in the layer's space, or comp space (`space: "comp"`, the default for a new layer).
  - `closed` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `fill` string or array or boolean, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1), or false for none
  - `fillAngle` json, deg
  - `fillBlend` string, a blend mode name (normal, multiply, …)
  - `fillGradient` array
  - `fillOpacity` number, percent, 0 to 100
  - `fillType` string, one of `none` | `solid` | `linear` | `radial`
  - `inTangents` array[], [[x, y], …]
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string
  - `outTangents` array[], [[x, y], …]
  - `space` string, one of `comp` | `layer`
  - `stroke` string or array or boolean, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1), or false for none
  - `strokeAngle` json
  - `strokeBlend` string, a blend mode name (normal, multiply, …)
  - `strokeGradient` json
  - `strokeOpacity` number, percent, 0 to 100
  - `strokeType` string, one of `none` | `solid` | `linear` | `radial`
  - `strokeWidth` number, default the Tools bar's, shape.toolOptions
  - `vertices` array
- `shape.fillStroke` (writes): The toolbar's Fill and Stroke options with shape layers selected (as in After Effects, they change the layers' fills and strokes): `fill` sets every Fill's colour, `stroke` every Stroke's, `strokeWidth` every stroke's width. A stroke colour or a width above 0 gives the paths that have no stroke one.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `fill` string, a colour such as #rrggbb
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `merge` string
  - `stroke` string, a colour such as #rrggbb
  - `strokeWidth` number
- `shape.dashes.add` (writes): Adds a dash/gap pair to a shape stroke (`prop` = the stroke's uid): the first call turns dashes on (Dash 10), later ones add Dash 2/Gap 2 and Dash 3/Gap 3, up to three pairs.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `prop` integer, stroke uid
- `shape.dashes.remove` (writes): Removes the last dash/gap pair from a shape stroke (`prop` = the stroke's uid); removing the last one turns dashes off.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `prop` integer, stroke uid
- `shape.stroke.taper` (writes): Sets a shape stroke's taper (`prop` = stroke uid): `startLength`/`endLength` (in `units` pixels or percent), `startWidth`/`endWidth` %, and `startEase`/`endEase` %, so the line thins toward its ends.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `endEase` number, (%)
  - `endLength` number
  - `endWidth` number, (%)
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `prop` integer, stroke uid
  - `startEase` number, (%)
  - `startLength` number
  - `startWidth` number, (%)
  - `units` string, one of `pixels` | `percent`, pixels|percent
- `shape.stroke.wave` (writes): Makes a shape stroke wavy (`prop` = stroke uid): `amount` %, `wavelength` (pixels) or `cycles` per `units`, and `phase` degrees.
  - `amount` number, %
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `cycles` number
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `phase` number, °
  - `prop` integer, stroke uid
  - `units` string, one of `pixels` | `cycles`
  - `wavelength` number
- `shape.newShape` (writes): Draws a shape as the shape tools do: `kind` of `size` at `position` goes into the selected shape layer's contents (or `layer`'s) as a new group, else into a new shape layer, painted with the Tools bar's Fill and Stroke (shape.toolOptions) unless given here, gradients included (`fillGradient`, `fillAngle`). Returns {layer, group}.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `fill` string or array or boolean, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1), or false for none
  - `fillAngle` json, deg
  - `fillBlend` string, a blend mode name (normal, multiply, …)
  - `fillGradient` array
  - `fillOpacity` number, percent, 0 to 100
  - `fillType` string, one of `none` | `solid` | `linear` | `radial`
  - `kind` string, one of `rect` | `rounded` | `ellipse` | `polygon` | `star`
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string, a new layer's
  - `position` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `size` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `space` string, one of `comp` | `layer`
  - `stroke` string or array or boolean, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1), or false for none
  - `strokeAngle` json
  - `strokeBlend` string, a blend mode name (normal, multiply, …)
  - `strokeGradient` json
  - `strokeOpacity` number, percent, 0 to 100
  - `strokeType` string, one of `none` | `solid` | `linear` | `radial`
  - `strokeWidth` number, default the Tools bar's, shape.toolOptions
- `shape.toolOptions` (writes): The Tools bar's options for the shape tools and the Pen: Tool Creates Shape / Tool Creates Mask (`createsMask`) and the Fill and Stroke new shapes get (the keys of [`paint_p`]); `reset` restores the defaults first. Reports the options.
  - `createsMask` boolean, Tool Creates Mask with a shape layer selected
  - `fill` string or array or boolean, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1), or false for none
  - `fillAngle` json, deg
  - `fillBlend` string, blend mode
  - `fillGradient` array
  - `fillType` string, one of `none` | `solid` | `linear` | `radial`
  - `reset` boolean
  - `stroke` string or array or boolean, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1), or false for none
  - `strokeAngle` json
  - `strokeBlend` string, a blend mode name (normal, multiply, …)
  - `strokeGradient` json
  - `strokeOpacity` number, percent, 0 to 100
  - `strokeType` string, one of `none` | `solid` | `linear` | `radial`
  - `strokeWidth` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `keys.setLabel` (writes): Sets the label colour of the selected keyframes: `label` a colour name, 0–16, or none. Returns the label and how many keys changed; it only marks keys, motion is unchanged.
  - `label` string, name|none|0–16
- `keys.selectLabelGroup` (writes): Select every keyframe that shares a label with a selected keyframe, on the selected or all layers. `visible` (property uids revealed in the Timeline) limits the "Visible Keyframes" scopes; without it every property counts as visible.
  - `scope` string, one of `selected` | `all` | `visibleSelected` | `visibleAll`
  - `visible` json[], [prop uid]
- `keys.transform` (writes): Transform the selected keys: times scale about `timeAnchor` (comp seconds, default the first selected key) by `timeScale` and move by `timeOffset`; values scale about `valueAnchor` by `valueScale` and move by `valueOffset` (every dimension, or only `dim`). Times land on frames.
  - `dim` array, one of several alternative parameters
  - `dims` array, one of several alternative parameters
  - `fromStart` boolean, with merge: values are the whole transform since the drag started
  - `merge` string
  - `timeAnchor` number, comp s
  - `timeOffset` number, s
  - `timeScale` number
  - `valueAnchor` number
  - `valueOffset` number
  - `valueScale` number
- `keys.setSpatialTangents` (writes): Spatial tangents of one key of a spatial property (motion path handles), relative to the key value. Setting one side only mirrors it to the other unless `break` is true; the key stops being auto Bezier.
  - `break` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `in` number[], [dx, dy, dz]
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `out` number
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number, layer s
- `file.findMissing` (writes): Finds what the project lacks: `what` footage (missing files, also selected in the project), effects (unknown effect ids per layer) or fonts. Returns the list; changes nothing.
  - `query` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `rescan` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `what` string, one of `footage` | `effects` | `fonts`
- `footage.check` (writes): Looks for the file of every footage item (or of `items`) and flags the ones that are missing; runs in the background unless `wait`.
  - `items` integer[]
  - `wait` boolean
- `footage.reloadChanged` (writes): Reloads the footage whose file changed on disk since it was last seen (size or modification time); files seen for the first time are only remembered. Answers {files, reloaded}.
  - `item` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `items` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `script.run` (writes): run JavaScript (the After Effects scripting object model: `app.project`, comps, layers, properties…) and report `{ok, result, output, error}`; script errors are reported in `error` (with line and column), not as a command failure.
  - `code` string, JavaScript: app, app.project, CompItem, Layer, Property… like After Effects scripting
  - `console` boolean, Script Console context
  - `name` string
- `file.timelineFormats` (writes): The formats, for agents and the export dialog. No parameters.
- `comp.responsiveTime` (writes): Responsive Design — Time: protected comp markers for an intro, an outro or the work area.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `op` string, one of `intro` | `outro` | `workArea`
- `file.watchFolder.poll` (writes): Checks the watched folder (or `folder`) now and renders newly arrived projects; returns each project's state (done or failed) and its render items' status and outputs.
  - `folder` file, default: the watched one
- `paths.pointsFollowNulls` (writes): Creates a null for every vertex of a path (or Position/Advanced puppet `pins`) and adds expressions so the path follows the nulls; move the nulls to animate the shape. Returns the nulls.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `pin` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `pins` array
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `paths.nullsFollowPoints` (writes): Creates a null for every vertex of a path (`layer` plus `path`/`prop`), or for `pins` of a puppet, with expressions so each null follows its point. Use to attach layers to path points. Returns the nulls.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `pin` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `pins` array
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `paths.tracePath` (writes): Creates a null that moves along a path (`layer` plus `path`/`prop`) driven by a Progress slider keyed 0→100% over the path's span; `loop` repeats it. Returns the null; parent layers to it to follow the path.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `loop` boolean
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `comp.vr.environments` (reads): Lists the VR environments in the project: output comp, name, cube map, each face's comp and camera, and the current view orientation [x, y, z] degrees. No parameters.
- `comp.vr.setView` (writes): Turns all six face cameras of a VR environment together: `orientation` [x, y, z] degrees, or `pan` (Y), `tilt` (X), `roll` (Z). `comp` names the environment's output, cube map or a face comp.
  - `comp` integer, an environment's output / cube map / face comp
  - `orientation` number[], [x
  - `pan` number
  - `roll` json
  - `tilt` number
- `app.about` (reads): Editor window only: shows the About box. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing. No parameters.
- `app.settings` (reads): Editor window only: opens Settings at `page` (general, previews, import, export, audio, disk, memory, 3d, scripting…). Headless sessions accept it and change nothing.
  - `page` string, general|startup|project|composition|previews|appearance|grids|labels|type|import|export|audio|disk|memory|video|3d|scripting
- `app.gpuInfo` (reads): Editor window only: shows the GPU information dialog. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; app.capabilities reports whether GPU rendering is on. No parameters.
- `app.hide` (reads): Editor window only: hides the application (macOS). Headless sessions accept it and change nothing. No parameters.
- `app.hideOthers` (reads): Editor window only: hides other applications (macOS). Headless sessions accept it and change nothing. No parameters.
- `app.showAll` (reads): Editor window only: shows all hidden applications (macOS). Headless sessions accept it and change nothing. No parameters.
- `app.quit` (reads): Editor window only: quits the application. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; the host closes documents. No parameters.
- `app.templates` (reads): Editor window only: opens the render settings or output module templates (`kind`). Headless sessions accept it and change nothing.
  - `kind` string, one of `renderSettings` | `outputModule`
- `playback.scrubAudio` (reads): Editor window only: turns audio while scrubbing on or off. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `time` number, s, default the current time
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `view.panelBackground` (reads): Frontend-only: changes the viewer panel's background colour (not the comp background; use comp.settings for that). Headless sessions do nothing.
  - `color` string, black|darkGray|mediumGray|lightGray|white|custom|#hex
  - `pick` boolean, default `true`
- `window.panel` (reads): Frontend-only: shows or focuses an editor panel. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing.
  - `panel` string, one of `project` | `effectControls` | `composition` | `layer` | `timeline` | `info` | `audio` | `preview` | `effectsPresets` | `properties` | `character` | `paragraph` | `align` | `tracker` | `wiggler` | `smoother` | `motionSketch` | `paint` | `brushes` | `renderQueue` | `flowchart` | `history` | `markers` | `tools` | `scopes` | `footage` | `mediaBrowser` | `metadata` | `progress` | `contentAwareFill` | `createNullsFromPaths` | `vrCompEditor`
  - `redo` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `steps` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `window.workspace` (reads): Frontend-only: switches the editor to a named workspace layout. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing.
  - `name` string, Default|Standard|Small Screen|Animation|Effects|Motion Tracking|Paint|Text|Minimal|All Panels
- `project.deleteWithoutConfirmation` (writes): Editor window only: deletes the selected project items without the confirmation dialog. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; check project.usage first. No parameters.
- `track.new` (writes): Adds a tracker to `layer`: `kind` transform, stabilize, affine, perspective or raw, tracking `position`, `rotation` and `scale` as set, applied to `target`. Returns the tracker.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `kind` string, one of `transform` | `stabilize` | `affine` | `perspective` | `raw`
  - `layer` integer
  - `position` number
  - `rotation` number
  - `scale` number
  - `target` integer or string, layer
- `track.select` (writes): Makes a tracker current (`tracker` uid, name or #n on `layer`); track.* commands without `tracker` act on it.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `tracker` integer or string, uid|name|#n
- `track.setType` (writes): Changes the current tracker's type (`kind` transform, stabilize, affine, perspective, raw) and which of `position`, `rotation`, `scale` it tracks, adding or removing track points as needed.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `kind` string, one of `transform` | `stabilize` | `affine` | `perspective` | `raw`
  - `layer` integer
  - `position` number
  - `rotation` number
  - `scale` number
  - `tracker` integer or string
- `track.setTarget` (writes): Sets the layer the tracker's result is applied to (`target`, or null); a stabilize tracker can only apply to the tracked layer.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `target` integer or string, layer|null
  - `tracker` integer or string
- `track.options` (writes): Sets the current tracker's options: `channel` rgb, luminance or saturation, `blur`, `enhance`, `subpixel`, `adaptEveryFrame`, confidence `threshold` % and the low-confidence `action` (continue, stop, extrapolate, adapt).
  - `action` string, one of `continue` | `stop` | `extrapolate` | `adapt`
  - `adaptEveryFrame` boolean
  - `blur` number, px, 0 = off
  - `channel` string, one of `rgb` | `luminance` | `saturation`
  - `colorized` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `enhance` boolean
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string
  - `subpixel` boolean
  - `threshold` number, %
  - `toggle` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `trackShape` boolean
  - `tracker` integer or string
- `track.setPoint` (writes): Moves or resizes track point `point` (1-based) at `time`: feature `center` or `move` [dx, dy], `featureSize`, `searchOffset`, `searchSize` and `attachOffset`, in layer pixels. Place points on high-contrast features before analyzing.
  - `attachOffset` number[]
  - `center` number[]
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `featureSize` number[]
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `move` number[], [dx, dy]
  - `point` integer, 1-based
  - `searchOffset` number[]
  - `searchSize` number[]
  - `time` number, s
  - `tracker` integer or string
- `track.analyze` (writes): Tracks the current tracker's track points through the footage: `direction` forward (default), backward or one frame either way, between `start` and `end` seconds; runs in the background, `wait` blocks. Then track.apply writes the result.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `direction` string, one of `forward` | `backward` | `frameForward` | `frameBackward`
  - `end` number, s
  - `layer` integer
  - `start` number, s
  - `tracker` integer or string
  - `wait` boolean, block until done
- `track.stop` (writes): Stops the motion tracking, mask tracking or warp stabilizer analysis that is running; results so far are kept. Returns {stopped}. No parameters.
- `track.apply` (writes): Applies a tracker's motion (`tracker` on `layer`, default the active one) to its target layer or effect point; `dimensions` xy, x or y.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `dimensions` string, xy|x|y
  - `layer` integer
  - `tracker` integer or string
- `track.reset` (writes): Resets a tracker (`tracker`, default the active one) on `layer`: its track points go back to their default places and their tracked data is cleared.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `tracker` integer or string
- `track.delete` (writes): Deletes a tracker (`tracker`, default the active one) from `layer`.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `tracker` integer or string
- `track.editTargetDialog` (writes): Editor window only: opens the Motion Target dialog. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; use track.setTarget. No parameters.
- `track.optionsDialog` (writes): Editor window only: opens the Motion Tracker Options dialog. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; use track.options. No parameters.
- `track.status` (reads): Returns tracking state: whether tracking, mask tracking or warp stabilizing runs and its progress, and for the current tracker its track points (center, feature and search sizes, key counts) and the layer's trackers.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `tracker` integer or string
- `track.maskMethod` (writes): Sets the default mask tracking method track.mask uses: position, positionScale, positionScaleRotation, positionScaleRotationSkew, perspective, faceOutline or faceDetailed.
  - `method` string, one of `position` | `positionScale` | `positionScaleRotation` | `positionScaleRotationSkew` | `perspective` | `faceOutline` | `faceDetailed`
- `track.extractFaceMeasurements` (writes): Extract & Copy Face Measurements: measure the Face Track Points at every keyed time, key them into the layer's Face Measurements effect and put those keys on the keyframe clipboard.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `wait` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `mask.interpolate` (writes): Fills the time between two Mask Path keyframes (`times` [from, to] seconds, default the selected keys) with in-between keys that morph the shape smoothly; options set the key rate, vertex matching and bending resistance.
  - `addVertices` boolean or number or string, n|false
  - `addVerticesUnit` string, pixels|total|percent
  - `bendingResistance` number, 0-100
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `firstVerticesMatch` json
  - `keyframeFields` json
  - `keyframeRate` number or string, n|auto
  - `layer` integer
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `linearVertexPaths` json
  - `mask` integer
  - `matchingMethod` string, one of `auto` | `curve` | `polyline`
  - `oneToOne` json
  - `quality` number, 0-100
  - `times` number[], [from, to]; s; default the selected Mask Path keys
- `mask.interpolationOptions` (writes): Sets the default options mask.interpolate uses (keyframe rate, linear vertex paths, bending resistance, quality, added vertices, matching method). Returns the options; changes no masks.
  - `addVertices` boolean or number or string, n|false
  - `addVerticesUnit` string, pixels|total|percent
  - `bendingResistance` number
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `firstVerticesMatch` json
  - `keyframeFields` json
  - `keyframeRate` number or string, n|auto
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `linearVertexPaths` json
  - `matchingMethod` string, one of `auto` | `curve` | `polyline`
  - `oneToOne` json
  - `quality` number
- `warp.analyze` (writes): Starts Warp Stabilizer analysis for a layer's Warp Stabilizer effect (`layer`, `effect` uid, name or index; default: first found). `wait` blocks until done and includes warp.status. Returns {layer, effect, frames, running, progress}.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string, uid|name|index
  - `layer` integer
  - `wait` boolean, block until done
- `warp.cancel` (writes): Stops the running Warp Stabilizer analysis; only enabled while one runs. Returns {stopped}. Analysis already stored on the effect stays. No parameters.
- `warp.status` (reads): Reports Warp Stabilizer progress {running, progress, banner} and, for a layer's Warp Stabilizer effect, whether it is analyzed or pending, frame count, size and the stabilization plan at the current frame. Read-only.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
- `camera.analyze` (writes): Runs (or continues) analysis of a 3D Camera Tracker effect on `layer` (`effect` by uid, name or index); `wait: true` blocks until done. Check progress with camera.solveStatus.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string, uid|name|index
  - `layer` integer
  - `wait` boolean, block until done
- `camera.cancel` (writes): Stops the 3D Camera Tracker analysis or solve that is running; returns {stopped}. Enabled only while one runs. No parameters.
- `camera.solveStatus` (reads): Returns the 3D Camera Tracker state: running, progress and banner text, and for `layer`/`effect` whether it is pending, analyzed and solved. Read it after camera.analyze before creating layers.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
- `camera.points` (reads): Returns the solved 3D Camera Tracker points visible at `time` (comp seconds, default now): id, comp and layer position, depth, world position, error, colour, selected. Fails before a solve.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
  - `time` number, comp seconds
- `camera.selectPoints` (reads): Selects 3D Camera Tracker points by id (`points`); `add` adds to the selection, `toggle` flips each. Use before camera.setGroundPlane or camera.createFromSolve.
  - `add` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `points` integer[]
  - `time` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `toggle` boolean
- `camera.createFromSolve` (writes): Create Text / Solid / Null / Shadow Catcher (and Light) on the target, plus the 3D Tracker Camera when the tracker has none yet — one undo step.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `kind` string, text|solid|null|shadowCatcher|camera
  - `layer` integer
  - `multiple` boolean
  - `points` integer[], default: selected
  - `target` object, {center, normal, size?} (comp world); comp world
  - `time` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `camera.create` (writes): Creates the 3D Tracker Camera layer from a solved 3D Camera Tracker on `layer` (`effect` picks the tracker), as camera.createFromSolve does for the camera alone. Needs a finished solve.
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
- `camera.setGroundPlane` (writes): Sets the solved 3D Camera Tracker's ground plane and origin from three or more track points (`points`, default the selected ones) at the current frame; created layers then sit on that plane. Fails if the points don't define a plane.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
  - `points` integer[], default: selected
  - `time` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `camera.deletePoints` (writes): Delete points (and, with Auto-delete Points Across Time, the points of other tracks on the same 3D feature), then re-solve.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
  - `points` integer[], default: selected
  - `time` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `wait` boolean
- `roto.stroke` (writes): Paints a Rotoscope Brush stroke on `layer` at layer `frame` (default now): `kind` fg (foreground, default), bg, refine or refineErase, `points` [[x, y]] in layer pixels, `radius`. Adds the Rotoscope Brush effect if needed, then segments the frame.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer
  - `frame` integer, layer frame; default current
  - `kind` string, one of `fg` | `bg` | `refine` | `refineErase`
  - `layer` integer
  - `points` array[], layer pixels
  - `radius` number, layer px; default the tool's diameter / 2
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `roto.propagate` (writes): Propagates the Rotoscope Brush segmentation from its stroked base frame `direction` forward, backward or both (default) across the span, extended to layer frame `to` if given; runs in the background, `wait` blocks until done.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `direction` string, one of `forward` | `backward` | `both`
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `end` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `start` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `to` number, layer frame: extend the span
  - `wait` boolean, block until done
- `roto.span` (writes): Sets the frames the Rotoscope Brush segmentation covers: `start` and `end` in layer frames, kept around the stroked frames. Fails when there are no strokes or the Rotoscope Brush is frozen.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `end` number, layer frames
  - `layer` integer
  - `start` number
- `roto.freeze` (writes): Freeze Frame: time remapping holding the current source frame for the whole layer.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
  - `wait` boolean
- `roto.unfreeze` (writes): Unfreezes a layer's Rotoscope Brush so its strokes and span can be edited again (frozen mattes are cached and not recomputed). Returns {frozen: false}.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
- `roto.clearStrokes` (writes): Removes Rotoscope Brush strokes from `layer`'s Rotoscope Brush effect: all, only those on layer `frame`, or only one `kind`. Fails while the Rotoscope Brush is frozen.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `frame` integer, only this layer frame
  - `kind` string
  - `layer` integer
- `roto.cancel` (writes): Stops the Rotoscope Brush propagation running in the background; frames done so far are kept. No parameters.
- `roto.options` (writes): Sets Rotoscope Brush tool options: brush `diameter` and `refineDiameter` (px), the viewer `view` (alphaBoundary, alpha, alphaOverlay, none), overlay and boundary colours and opacity, and `autoPropagate`. Returns them; the project is unchanged.
  - `autoPropagate` boolean
  - `boundaryColor` number[], [r, g, b]
  - `diameter` number
  - `overlayColor` number[], [r, g, b]
  - `overlayOpacity` number
  - `refineDiameter` number
  - `view` string, one of `alphaBoundary` | `alpha` | `alphaOverlay` | `none`
- `roto.status` (reads): Returns the Rotoscope Brush state for `layer`: running and progress, base frame, span, stroke count and frames, frozen, frame limits; for `frame` also its matte coverage, with `matte` the RLE matte and `compareTo` an IoU against another matte.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `compareTo` string, RLE matte to report the IoU against
  - `compute` boolean, compute the frame if needed
  - `effect` integer or string
  - `frame` integer, layer frame: also report its matte
  - `layer` integer
  - `matte` boolean, include the matte (RLE, base64); RLE, base64
- `paint.stroke` (writes): Paints one stroke on a layer (adds a Paint effect if needed): `kind` brush, clone or eraser, `points` [[x, y, pressure]] in effect space, at `time`, with colour, size and opacity options; `durationMode` writeOn animates it.
  - `angle` number
  - `channels` string, one of `RGBA` | `RGB` | `Alpha`
  - `clonePosition` number[]
  - `cloneSource` integer or string, layer id
  - `cloneTime` number, s
  - `cloneTimeShift` number, (s)
  - `color` number[], [r, g, b, a]
  - `customFrames` integer
  - `diameter` number
  - `duration` number, s, drawing time for Write On
  - `durationMode` string, one of `constant` | `writeOn` | `singleFrame` | `custom`
  - `eraseMode` string, one of `layerSourceAndPaint` | `paintOnly` | `lastStrokeOnly`
  - `flow` number
  - `flowPressure` boolean
  - `frame` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `hardness` number
  - `kind` string, one of `brush` | `clone` | `eraser`
  - `layer` integer
  - `lockSourceTime` boolean
  - `minSize` number
  - `mode` string
  - `opacity` number
  - `opacityPressure` boolean
  - `points` array, [[x,y,pressure?],…] (effect space); effect space
  - `roundness` number
  - `sizePressure` boolean
  - `spacing` number
  - `time` number, (s) | frame?
- `paint.options` (writes): Sets the paint tool options later paint.stroke calls use: colour, opacity, flow, mode, channels, duration mode, brush tip (diameter, angle, roundness, hardness, spacing), pressure, clone source and offset; `reset` restores defaults. Returns them.
  - `aligned` boolean
  - `angle` number
  - `background` string or array
  - `channels` string
  - `cloneOffset` json[]
  - `clonePoint` json
  - `clonePreset` integer
  - `cloneSource` number
  - `cloneTime` number
  - `cloneTimeShift` number
  - `color` string
  - `customFrames` integer
  - `diameter` number
  - `durationMode` json
  - `eraseMode` json
  - `flow` number
  - `flowPressure` boolean
  - `hardness` number
  - `lockSourceTime` boolean
  - `minSize` number
  - `mode` string
  - `name` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `opacity` number
  - `opacityPressure` boolean
  - `overlayDifference` boolean
  - `overlayOpacity` number
  - `preset` string
  - `reset` boolean
  - `roundness` number
  - `showOverlay` boolean
  - `sizePressure` boolean
  - `spacing` number
- `paint.brushPreset` (writes): Chooses a brush preset for later paint strokes by index or name (`preset`); without `preset` returns the preset names. Paint tool state only; the project is unchanged.
  - `name` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `preset` number or string, index | name
- `paint.setCloneSource` (writes): Sets the clone stamp source to `point` [x, y] (effect space) on `layer` for later paint.stroke calls with kind clone. Paint tool state only.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `point` number[]
- `paint.removeStroke` (writes): Find a stroke group by uid or name across the layer's Paint effects.
  - `layer` integer
  - `stroke` integer or string, uid | name
- `paint.presets` (reads): Lists the brush presets with index, name, diameter, angle, roundness, hardness and spacing. No parameters.
- `puppet.addPin` (writes): Adds a puppet pin to `layer` at `position` [x, y] (effect space): `kind` position (default), advanced, bend, starch or overlap; creates a mesh (Puppet effect) where none covers that point. Returns the pin.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `density` number
  - `expansion` number
  - `frame` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `kind` string, one of `position` | `advanced` | `bend` | `starch` | `overlap`
  - `layer` integer
  - `mesh` integer, uid
  - `newMesh` boolean
  - `position` number[], effect space
  - `time` number, (s) | frame?
  - `triangles` number
- `puppet.movePin` (writes): Moves a puppet `pin` (uid or name) to `position` [x, y] at `time`, keying it, which deforms the mesh; starch and overlap pins move their region instead. Bend pins have no position (use puppet.setPin).
  - `frame` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `pin` integer, uid | name
  - `position` number[]
  - `time` number, one of several alternative parameters
- `puppet.setPin` (writes): Sets a puppet pin's values at `time`: `position`, `scale` %, `rotation` °, `amount` %, `extent` px, `inFront`, keyed when animated. Which apply depends on the pin kind.
  - `amount` number, %
  - `extent` number, (px)
  - `frame` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `inFront` json
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `pin` integer, uid | name
  - `position` number
  - `rotation` number, °
  - `scale` number, %
  - `time` number, one of several alternative parameters
- `puppet.removePin` (writes): Deletes puppet pins: `pin` or `pins` by uid or name, default the selected pins. Returns how many were removed.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `pin` integer, uid | name
  - `pins` array
- `puppet.selectPins` (writes): Select pins (the viewer's click / Shift-click on a pin). Plain: only these pins; `add`: add them; `toggle`: flip each. An empty `pins` deselects every pin.
  - `add` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `pin` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `pins` array, [] deselects
  - `toggle` boolean
- `puppet.mesh` (writes): Sets mesh options (`density`, `expansion`, `triangles`) for `mesh` on `layer`, or the defaults for new meshes when no layer is given; `showMesh` toggles the mesh overlay. With no options returns the current ones.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `density` number
  - `expansion` number
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string
  - `mesh` integer, uid
  - `showMesh` boolean
  - `time` number
  - `triangles` number
- `puppet.info` (reads): Returns a layer's puppet meshes at `time`: each mesh's outline, triangle and vertex counts, rest and deformed mesh, and its pins with kind, rest and current position. Empty without a Puppet effect.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `frame` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `time` number, one of several alternative parameters
- `puppet.recordPin` (writes): Puppet tool Record mode (⌘/Ctrl-drag a pin): the pin's drag, sampled in real time, becomes Position keyframes at the comp frame rate from the current time on, replacing the keys in the recorded span.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `pin` integer, uid | name
  - `pins` array, more pins that move by the same displacement
  - `samples` array, t = seconds since the drag began, effect space
  - `smoothing` number, Record Options
  - `speed` number, %, Record Options
  - `start` number, s, default current time
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `puppet.follow` (writes): Follow-Through (hair, cloth, tails, overlapping action): each follower pin trails the leader pin's motion by a delay, through an expression on its Position. The followers nearest the leader trail least; with `cascade` the k-th nearest trails k × `delay`, otherwise all trail by `delay`.
  - `amount` number, %, 100
  - `cascade` boolean, true: the k-th nearest pin trails k × delay
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `delay` number, s, 0.1
  - `layer` integer
  - `leader` integer or string, uid | name (default: the first selected pin)
  - `pin` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `pins` array, default: the other selected pins
- `puppet.recordOptions` (writes): Record Options (the Puppet tool's Record Options… dialog): `speed`, `smoothing`, `useDraftDeformation`, `showMesh`. Returns the options.
  - `showMesh` boolean
  - `smoothing` number, 0-100
  - `speed` number, %, 100
  - `useDraftDeformation` boolean
- `liquify.stroke` (writes): Paints one Liquify stroke on a layer's Liquify effect: `tool` warp, twirl, pucker, bloat, turbulence, reconstruction and others, `points` [[x, y]] in effect space, `size`, `pressure`, `jitter`, at `time`. Add the Liquify effect first.
  - `cloneOffset` number[], [dx, dy]
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer, uid
  - `frame` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `jitter` number, 1-100
  - `layer` integer
  - `points` array[], effect space
  - `pressure` number, 1-100
  - `size` number
  - `time` number, (s) | frame?
  - `tool` string, one of `warp` | `turbulence` | `twirlClockwise` | `twirlCounterclockwise` | `pucker` | `bloat` | `shiftPixels` | `reflection` | `clone` | `reconstruction` | `freeze` | `thaw`
- `liquify.clear` (writes): Clears the mesh of a Liquify effect (`effect` uid, default the first) on `layer`, removing all its distortion.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `effect` integer, uid
  - `layer` integer
- `prefs.get` (reads): Returns one setting by `key` (e.g. general.undoLevels), or all settings when omitted. List the pages and keys with prefs.pages.
  - `key` string, e.g. general.undoLevels (omit for all settings); omit for all settings
- `prefs.set` (reads): Changes settings: `key` and `value` (e.g. general.undoLevels), or several at once as `values` {key: value}. Saved to the preferences; scripts can't change scripting permissions. Affects the app, not the project file.
  - `key` string
  - `value` string
  - `values` object
- `prefs.reset` (reads): Resets the settings on `page` (general, labels, project…) or all settings to their defaults; script permissions stay as the user set them when a script calls it.
  - `page` string, general|labels|project|…
- `prefs.open` (reads): Editor window only: opens Settings at `page`. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; use prefs.get and prefs.set.
  - `page` string, general|startup|project|composition|previews|appearance|grids|labels|type|import|export|audio|disk|memory|video|3d|scripting
- `prefs.pages` (reads): Lists the settings pages and the setting keys on each, for prefs.get and prefs.set. No parameters.
- `shortcuts.list` (reads): Lists commands with their keyboard shortcuts; `query` filters by words in label, command or keys, `keys` finds what a key combination does, `assigned: true` only bound commands.
  - `assigned` boolean
  - `keys` string
  - `query` string
- `shortcuts.set` (reads): Binds keys to a `command` (with `params` when the binding passes some): `keys` "Cmd+Shift+K", a list, or null to unbind. Editing the default preset creates a custom copy. Returns keys and conflicts.
  - `command` string
  - `keys` string, "Cmd+Shift+K" | [keys] | null
  - `params` json
- `shortcuts.reset` (reads): Resets one `command`'s shortcut to its default, or the whole active preset when no command is given.
  - `command` string
  - `params` json
- `shortcuts.preset` (reads): Manages keyboard shortcut presets: `op` select (`name`), new, duplicate (`from`), delete or rename (`newName`).
  - `from` string
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string
  - `op` string, one of `select` | `new` | `duplicate` | `delete` | `rename`
- `shortcuts.export` (reads): Exports a keyboard shortcut preset (`preset`, default the active one) as JSON, written to `path` when given, else returned.
  - `path` file
  - `preset` string
- `shortcuts.import` (reads): Imports a keyboard shortcut preset from `path` or an exported document in `preset`, under `name`. Returns the preset name.
  - `name` string
  - `path` file, exported document; one of several alternative parameters
  - `preset` number or string, exported document; one of several alternative parameters
- `shortcuts.conflicts` (reads): Lists keyboard shortcut conflicts in the active preset: each command, its keys, and the command and scope it collides with. No parameters.
- `file.openRecent` (writes): Opens a recent project, replacing the current one: `path`, or `index` into the recent list (default the newest). A project that no longer exists is dropped from the list and the call fails.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `path` file, one of several alternative parameters
- `file.autoSave` (writes): Saves an auto-save copy of the project now, to the auto-save folder; the open project's own file is not overwritten. Returns {path}. No parameters.
- `file.recoveryInfo` (reads): Returns auto-save status: the last auto-save path, the newest auto-save on disk, the auto-save folder and the recent projects list. Changes nothing. No parameters.
- `edit.history` (writes): Edit ▸ History: `{steps: n}` undoes the last n steps (the entry n−1 of the list), `{redo: n}` redoes n; without either, lists the steps (newest first).
  - `redo` integer
  - `steps` integer, undo n steps
- `file.importRecent` (writes): Imports a recently imported footage file again: `path`, or `index` into the recent list (default the newest), as file.import.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `path` file, one of several alternative parameters
- `anim.applyRecentPreset` (writes): Re-applies a recently used animation preset: `path`, or `index` into the recent list (default the newest), to `layers` or the selection, exactly as anim.applyPreset with that path.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); one of several alternative parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `path` file, one of several alternative parameters
- `file.executeFile` (writes): `File.execute()` from scripts (and agents): open a file with its default application. Needs Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network; with Warn User When Executing Files on, the frontend asks first (`confirmed: true` skips the question).
  - `confirmed` boolean
  - `path` file
- `view.assign3dShortcut` (reads): View ▸ Assign Shortcut to "<current 3D view>": F10, F11 or F12 switches to the view.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `slot` string, one of `F10` | `F11` | `F12`
- `window.assignWorkspaceShortcut` (reads): Window ▸ Assign Shortcut to "<workspace>" Workspace: Shift+F10, Shift+F11 or Shift+F12. The frontend fills in the current workspace.
  - `slot` string, Shift+F10|Shift+F11|Shift+F12
  - `workspace` string
- `help.systemInfo` (reads): Returns the system report: app name, version and build, OS, CPU architecture and core count, GPU, whether expressions, media import and the disk cache are available, and the plug-in count. Changes nothing. No parameters.
- `keys.applyEase` (writes): Eases every segment between consecutive keyframes of one property (`path` or `prop`; `from`/`to` in layer seconds limit the keys) with a named curve: snappy, out, smooth, swift, linear, or the overshoot landings settle, pop, reseat, fly (`bezier: [x1,y1,x2,y2]` for any CSS cubic-bezier). Curves become exact AE temporal ease (speed and influence); on a motion path an overshoot inserts a key at each turning point. Spring presets (crisp, lively, noBounce, cardFlip, or spring with damping/stiffness/mass) attach an expression that springs the motion into the last key. One undo step.
  - `bezier` number[], [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `damping` number
  - `from` number, seconds; layer time
  - `layer` integer or string, default the first selected layer
  - `mass` number
  - `merge` string
  - `path` string
  - `preset` string, one of `snappy` | `out` | `smooth` | `swift` | `settle` | `pop` | `reseat` | `fly` | `linear` | `crisp` | `lively` | `noBounce` | `cardFlip` | `spring`
  - `prop` integer
  - `stiffness` number
  - `to` number, seconds; layer time
- `keys.easePresets` (reads): Lists the ease presets keys.applyEase takes: curves (id, CSS bezier, when to use) and springs (id, damping, stiffness, mass, when to use). Read-only. No parameters.
- `camera.move` (writes): Adds a promo camera move from `start`: pushHover (the view pushes from 0.8x to 2.6x onto `target` in 18 frames while the rig turns 34 degrees Y and 8 X, hovers, then returns), craneRise (3x to 1x over 102 frames after a 1.5% anticipation push, rising), orbit (the rig turns `degrees` with continuous, monotone velocity through its keys) on a new camera parented to a 3D null at the target (target layers made 3D); or parallax: `layers` far to near pan at `speeds` 0.35/0.7/1.4 with blur 5 + 70% desaturation on the far one and blur 7 on the near one. One undo step; answers the camera and rig.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `degrees` number, degrees; orbit sweep, 30
  - `direction` number[], parallax, default [-1, 0]
  - `distance` number, pixels; parallax travel of a speed-1 layer, 600
  - `dx` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `dy` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `ease` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `farBlur` number, pixels; 5
  - `farDesaturate` number, 0.7
  - `frames` number, pushHover total 66, craneRise 102, orbit 90, parallax 90
  - `from` number, start scale: pushHover 0.8, craneRise 3
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, layer ids, names or #n
  - `motionBlur` boolean, moving layers get motion blur, shutter 180, 10 samples; default true
  - `name` string
  - `nearBlur` number, pixels; 7
  - `point` number[], comp px, instead of target
  - `preset` string, one of `pushHover` | `craneRise` | `orbit` | `parallax`
  - `pushFrames` number, pushHover in and out, 18
  - `rotX` number, degrees; pushHover 8, craneRise -8, orbit 0
  - `rotY` number, degrees; pushHover 34
  - `scale` number, pushHover 2.6, craneRise 1, orbit 1
  - `speeds` number[], parallax, default 0.35, 0.7, 1.4
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time; default the current time
  - `target` integer or string, the layer the camera works around
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `transition.iris` (writes): Iris carry: a circular mask on the incoming `layer` opens from `center` (a comp point, or the middle of a layer it follows) over `frames` (14) until it reaches the farthest corner, so the next scene opens out of a subject; an Iris slider keyed 0 to 1 with `ease` drives the mask path expression; `ring` adds a shape layer stroking the iris edge. One undo step.
  - `center` array or integer or string, [x, y] comp px, or a layer whose middle the iris follows
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `ease` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `feather` number, pixels; mask feather, default 0
  - `frames` number, default 14
  - `layer` integer or string, the incoming layer or precomp
  - `mask` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `ring` object or boolean, a stroke on the iris edge: {color?, width?} or true
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time; default the current time
- `transition.morphRect` (writes): Container-transform carry: the `from` layer's on-screen rectangle (with its corner radius) morphs into the `to` layer's rectangle over `frames` (18, smooth): both layers get a rounded-rectangle mask that follows the container and a cover scale and position keyed every frame, so the outgoing content scales and crops into the incoming one, which fades in inside the container over the last third. One undo step.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `ease` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `frames` number, default 18
  - `from` integer or string, the outgoing layer (its on-screen rectangle at start)
  - `motionBlur` boolean, default true
  - `radius` number or array, corner radius px: a number or [from, to]
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time; default the current time
  - `to` integer or string, the incoming layer (its rectangle at the end)
- `transition.zoomThrough` (writes): Zoom-through carry: the outgoing `layer` pushes into `target` with its scale keyed every frame in log space (ease-in) until the area of `size` px around the point fills the frame, then crosses over `blend` frames (the upper layer fades, the lower cuts) into `toLayer`, which continues from `overshoot` (1.25x) and settles to its own scale over `settleFrames`; motion blur on. One undo step.
  - `blend` number, frames the upper layer fades over once the frame is filled, default 2
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `ease` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `frames` number, the push, default 12
  - `layer` integer or string, the outgoing layer
  - `motionBlur` boolean, default true
  - `overshoot` number, incoming start scale, default 1.25
  - `settleEase` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `settleFrames` number, default 16
  - `size` number, pixels; the area around the target that fills the frame at the end of the push, default 48
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time; default the current time
  - `target` number[], [x, y] comp px: the point pushed into
  - `toLayer` integer or string, the incoming layer
- `layer.shake` (writes): Adds a deterministic decaying shake from `frame` (comp seconds) to a layer's position and rotation, or a camera's position, point of interest and Z rotation: `amplitude` px and `rotation` degrees falling off by exp(-decay t) at `frequency` Hz with phases from `seed`; zero before `frame`; written as an expression on top of the existing keys or expression. One undo step.
  - `amplitude` number, pixels; default 14
  - `camera` integer or string or boolean, a camera layer, or true for the comp's top camera
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `decay` number, per second: falls off as exp(-decay t), default 6
  - `frame` number, seconds; comp time of the hit; zero before it; default the current time
  - `frequency` json, Hz (default 12); default 12
  - `layer` integer or string, the layer (or camera layer) to shake
  - `quality` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `rotation` number, degrees; default 1.5
  - `seed` integer, default 1
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `layer.handheld` (writes): Adds a slow handheld float (two sines per axis) to a layer's or camera's position and rotation between `start` and `end`, `amount` px, easing in and out over `ramp` seconds and exactly zero inside every `holds` range; written as an expression on top of the existing keys or expression. One undo step.
  - `amount` number, pixels; default 6
  - `camera` integer or string or boolean, a camera layer, or true for the comp's top camera
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `end` number, seconds; default the comp's end
  - `holds` array[], [[from, to]] comp seconds where the float is exactly zero
  - `layer` integer or string, the layer (or camera layer) that floats
  - `quality` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `ramp` number, seconds; ease in and out of the float and of each hold, default 0.4
  - `rotation` number, degrees; default 0.4
  - `seed` integer, default 1
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time, default 0
- `layer.hop` (writes): Hops a layer along a 2D ballistic arc from where it is at `start` to `to`, `height` px above the start, over `frames`; stretches along the flight, lands with a squash of `squash` (the bottom stays on the ground) and rings out damped over `ringFrames`. Position and Scale keyed every frame. One undo step.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `frames` number, the flight, default 18
  - `height` number, pixels; apex above the straight line, default 160
  - `layer` integer or string, the layer that hops
  - `motionBlur` boolean, default true
  - `ringFrames` number, damped ring-out after landing, default 16
  - `squash` number, landing squash, 0.25 = 125 % wide / 75 % tall
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time; default the current time
  - `stretch` number, stretch along the flight, default 0.4 × squash
  - `to` number[], [x, y] landing position (comp px)
- `layer.gather` (writes): Gathers `layers` into a ring of `radius` around `center`: each flies along a spiral arc that sweeps about `arc` degrees into its slot, `stagger` frames after the one before, over `frames` with `ease`; Position keyed every frame, motion blur on. One undo step.
  - `arc` number, degrees; how far each spirals around, default 90; negative turns the other way
  - `center` number[], [x, y] ring centre (comp px)
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `ease` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `frames` number, each layer's flight, default 30
  - `layers` array, layer ids, names or #n
  - `motionBlur` boolean, default true
  - `radius` number, pixels; default 120
  - `stagger` number, frames between layers, default 2
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time; default the current time
- `light.spotlight` (writes): Darkens the comp (or `layers` and what is under them) except a soft hole that follows `target`: a black solid at `dim` (0.92) opacity whose Circle effects cut a core hole (softness 22 px) and a 15% spill (60 px); the radius goes from 400 to 300 px over `frames` (24) from `start` and then breathes +6% (`pulse`, `period`). One undo step; answers the new layer.
  - `color` string, a colour such as #rrggbb
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `dim` number, 0..1 darkness outside the light, default 0.92
  - `ease` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `frames` number, frames from the first radius to the second, default 24
  - `layers` array, layer ids, names or #n
  - `name` string
  - `period` number, seconds; breath length, default 2
  - `pulse` number, fraction the light breathes once settled, default 0.06
  - `radius` number or array, px: a number, or [from, to]
  - `softness` number, pixels; edge blur sigma, default 22
  - `spill` number, 0..1 light that leaks past the edge, default 0.15
  - `spillSoftness` number, pixels; default 60
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time; default the current time
  - `target` integer or string, the layer the light follows
- `light.sheen` (writes): Sweeps one specular band across a `layer` once: two CC Light Sweep effects (soft 0.14 and core 0.5 intensity, warm white, 115 degree CSS angle) clipped to the layer's alpha, driven by a Sheen Progress slider keyed 0 to 1 over `frames` (32) from `start` with the swift curve. One undo step.
  - `angle` number, degrees; CSS gradient angle, default 115
  - `color` string, a colour such as #rrggbb
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `core` number, narrow core intensity, default 0.5
  - `ease` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `frames` number, sweep length, default 32
  - `layer` integer or string, default the first selected layer
  - `soft` number, wide light intensity, default 0.14
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time; default the current time
  - `width` number, band width in layer widths, default 2
- `layer.liftShadow` (writes): Gives a `layer` a lift shadow driven by an Elevation slider (px): a tight contact Drop Shadow (opacity 12%/(1+e/24)) and a wide ambient one (opacity 8%+22%*min(e,64)/64), distance and softness growing with elevation. `elevation` static, or `to` reached `frames` after `start`, or `keys` [[comp s, elevation]]. One undo step; answers the effects added.
  - `color` string, a colour such as #rrggbb
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `direction` number, degrees; default 180, straight down
  - `ease` string or array, a curve name (snappy, out, smooth, swift, settle, pop, reseat, fly, linear) or [x1, y1, x2, y2]
  - `elevation` number, px, default 3
  - `frames` number, default 18
  - `keys` array[], [[comp seconds, elevation], …]
  - `layer` integer or string, default the first selected layer
  - `start` number, seconds; comp time
  - `to` number, elevation reached `frames` after `start`
- `templateProps.setPrimary` (writes): Makes `comp` the primary composition whose Graphics Templates controls the panel and templateProps.* commands edit by default. Changes no content.
  - `comp` integer or string
- `templateProps.setName` (writes): Sets the name the Graphics Templates panel and templates use for `comp`. Returns {comp, name}.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `name` string
- `templateProps.addMirror` (writes): Add a mirror of a property control (the same property shown again, e.g. in another group).
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `control` integer
  - `group` integer
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `name` string
- `templateProps.linkProperty` (writes): Make a property control drive another property too (same kind of value).
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `control` integer
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, default: the selected property; one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` integer, default: the selected property; one of several alternative parameters
- `templateProps.unlinkProperty` (writes): Disconnects one layer property (`layer` plus `path`/`prop`, default the selected property) from Graphics Templates control `control`; the control keeps its other links. Fails if that property isn't linked to it.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `control` integer
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, default: the selected property; one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` integer, default: the selected property; one of several alternative parameters
- `templateProps.addMedia` (writes): Media Replacement for a footage layer.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `group` integer
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string
- `templateProps.addGroup` (writes): Adds an empty group (`name`) to the Graphics Templates panel of `comp` at `index`; move controls into it with templateProps.move. Groups can't nest. Returns {control}.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `name` string
- `templateProps.addComment` (writes): Adds a comment entry with `text` to the Graphics Templates panel of `comp`, optionally inside group `group`. Returns {control}. Comments only label the panel; they drive nothing.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `group` integer
  - `text` string
- `templateProps.rename` (writes): Renames a Graphics Templates control (`control` id) in `comp` to `name`. The name is what instances of the comp show for that property.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `control` integer
  - `name` string
  - `text` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `templateProps.remove` (writes): Removes the control `control` (id) from the Template Properties of `comp` (default the active comp).
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `control` integer
