- `templateProps.move` (writes): Moves a Graphics Templates control (`control` id) into group `group` (null = top level) at `index`. Groups can't nest or contain themselves.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `control` integer
  - `group` integer, an id; null = top level
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `templateProps.soloSupported` (writes): Shows only the properties that can be added to Graphics Templates in the timeline (`on`, default toggles). Returns {on}; changes no content.
  - `on` boolean
- `templateProps.set` (writes): Set an instance's value for a control (`value`, or `item` for Media Replacement).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `control` integer, id|name
  - `item` integer, media; one of several alternative parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `value` string, media; one of several alternative parameters
- `templateProps.pushToComp` (writes): Push to Comp: write the instance's override values into the source comp's properties (and replaced media into the source layer), then drop the overrides.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `control` integer, default: all overridden
  - `layer` integer
- `templateProps.revert` (writes): Removes a precomp instance's overrides so its Template Properties follow the source comp again: `control` one, or all overridden ones by default, on `layer`. Clears their keys and expressions.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `control` integer, default: all overridden
  - `layer` integer
  - `supported` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `effect.editDropdown` (writes): Dropdown Menu Control ▸ Edit: the menu items of a dropdown (popup) property.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `items` string[]
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `templateProps.list` (reads): Returns the Graphics Templates of `comp`: its name, the primary comp, the solo state and every control (id, name, kind, group, linked properties); `supported: true` also lists the properties that could be added.
  - `comp` integer
  - `supported` boolean
- `templateProps.canAdd` (reads): Checks whether a property (`layer` plus `path` or `prop`) can be added to Graphics Templates, optionally `as` a given control type. Returns {ok, type, reason}; changes nothing.
  - `as` string
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `templateProps.instance` (reads): Returns the Template Properties of a precomp `layer`: each control of the source comp with its kind, current value at the current time and whether this instance overrides it.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
- `templateProps.templateInfo` (reads): Reads an .ectemplate file's manifest at `path` without importing it: its name, the template comp and the controls it exposes.
  - `path` file
- `expr.errors` (reads): Lists the expression errors in `comp` at `time` (seconds, default now): each failing property with layer, path and message, plus text lines like the error bar shows. Use after setting expressions with prop.setExpression.
  - `comp` integer
  - `time` number, s
- `expr.languageMenu` (reads): Returns the expression language menu: categories with each entry's label and the snippet it inserts. Use it to look up expression functions; changes nothing. No parameters.
- `file.createProxy` (writes): File ▸ Create Proxy ▸ Still / Movie: queue a half-resolution render of the composition whose post-render action sets the result as its proxy.
  - `comp` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `kind` string, one of `still` | `movie`
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `output` string, template; one of several alternative parameters
  - `path` file, template; one of several alternative parameters
  - `quality` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `resolution` number, default 0.5
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `file.useProxy` (writes): The Project panel's proxy switch: use the proxy (filled box) or the full-resolution source.
  - `item` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `items` integer[], one of several alternative parameters
  - `on` boolean
- `file.uninstallScript` (writes): Deletes the installed script or script panel `name` (file name with .jsx/.js) from the Scripts and Script Panels folders. Fails if it isn't installed.
  - `name` string
- `file.scripts.list` (reads): Lists the scripts and script panels available: name, whether it is a panel, and source (installed, sample or extension). Run one with file.runScript. No parameters.
- `window.scriptPanel` (reads): Window ▸ <script panel>: run the panel script (or bring its panel forward).
  - `name` string, a script in the Script Panels folder, e.g. `Layer Tools.jsx`
- `window.restoreScriptPanels` (reads): open the script panels that were open when Kition Motion last quit (frontends call it once at launch). Panels whose script is gone or fails are reported and forgotten; the others still open. No parameters.
- `script.settings.get` (reads): Reads a script setting (`section`, `key`) from the settings store, as the scripting API's app.settings.getSetting() does. Returns {have, value}.
  - `key` string
  - `section` json
- `script.settings.save` (writes): Saves a script setting (`section`, `key`, text `value`) in the settings store, as the scripting API's app.settings.saveSetting() does; it persists across sessions.
  - `key` string
  - `path` file, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `section` json
  - `value` string, text
- `scriptWindow.list` (reads): Lists the open script windows and panels: window id, title, kind (dialog, palette, window, panel), script, modal and size. No parameters.
- `scriptWindow.get` (reads): Returns a script window's controls (`window` id or title): its tree of controls with type, name, text, value, items, selection, bounds and enabled state.
  - `views` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `window` integer, id | title
- `scriptWindow.click` (writes): press a button / toggle a checkbox / pick a radio button.
  - `widget` integer or string, id | "#id" | properties.name | text
  - `window` integer, id | title
- `scriptWindow.set` (writes): Sets a control of a script window: `widget` (id or name) to `value` (text, number, bool, or a list item's index or text); `changing: true` sends a live update, as while dragging a slider.
  - `changing` boolean, a live update: each keystroke / slider step; fires onChanging only
  - `value` string, text | number | bool | item index | item text
  - `widget` json
  - `window` integer
- `scriptWindow.close` (writes): close a window (a dialog's `show()` returns `result`, default 2 = Cancel).
  - `result` json, a dialog's show() returns it; default 2 = Cancel
  - `window` integer
- `jobs.list` (reads): Returns the background jobs (renders, tracking, warp stabilizing, camera solves, roto) that are running with their progress, and the log of finished ones. Use with jobs.wait. No parameters.
- `jobs.cancel` (writes): Cancels running background work: `job` render, track, maskTrack, warp, camera, roto, task:<n> or all (default). Returns what was cancelled; finished results stay.
  - `job` string, render|track|maskTrack|warp|camera|roto|task:<n>|all
- `jobs.wait` (reads): Blocks until every background job (renders, tracking, solves) has finished, then returns the finished jobs log. Call after starting work you need the result of. No parameters.
- `mediaBrowser.list` (reads): Lists a folder (`path`, default the browser's current one): entries with name, kind and size, the parent folder, favorites, places and available actions; `importableOnly` hides other files.
  - `importableOnly` boolean
  - `path` file
- `mediaBrowser.go` (reads): Opens folder `path` (or ".." for the parent, default home) in the Media Browser and returns its listing, as mediaBrowser.list; `importableOnly` hides files that can't be imported.
  - `importableOnly` boolean
  - `path` file, folder | ".."
- `mediaBrowser.addFavorite` (writes): Adds the folder `path` (default the browser's current folder) to the Media Browser favorites. Changes no project.
  - `path` file
- `mediaBrowser.removeFavorite` (writes): Removes the folder `path` (default the current folder) from the Media Browser favorites.
  - `path` file
- `mediaBrowser.import` (writes): Imports files from the Media Browser (`paths`); a numbered still brings its image sequence unless `sequence: false`. `addToComp` with `time`, `index`, `position` also places them in the active comp as layer.addItem does.
  - `addToComp` boolean
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `paths` file
  - `position` number, where the layers go, as in layer.addItem
  - `sequence` boolean, default true: a numbered still brings its image sequence
  - `time` number
- `mediaBrowser.action` (writes): A browser-specific toolbar action (web: Open Folder…, Add Files…).
  - `action` string
- `mediaBrowser.fileInfo` (reads): Returns a file's info without importing it: kind, size, created and modified dates and, for video, image, audio or 3D files, its footage metadata (size, duration, frame rate, codec).
  - `path` file
- `item.metadata` (reads): Returns metadata for the project (name, path, item and comp counts, bit depth, working space, time display) and, when `item` (id or name) is given, for that item (type, size, label, comment and its own fields).
  - `item` integer, id|name
- `project.setProjectComment` (writes): Sets the project's own comment (Project panel). A note stored in the project file.
  - `comment` string
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `scopes.analyze` (reads): Analyses the comp's frame at `time`: `scope` waveform (RGB, luma, YC), vectorscope, histogram or parade, with `standard` rec601/709/2020; returns the scope data plus mean RGB and min, max and mean luma. Use to check exposure and colour.
  - `clamp` boolean
  - `comp` integer
  - `float` boolean
  - `frame` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `scope` string, one of `waveformRgb` | `waveformLuma` | `waveformYc` | `vectorscopeYuv` | `vectorscopeHls` | `histogram` | `paradeRgb` | `paradeYuv`
  - `size` number
  - `standard` string, one of `rec601` | `rec709` | `rec2020`
  - `time` number, one of several alternative parameters
- `footage.open` (writes): Opens the footage item `item` (id or name) in the Footage panel, at its first frame.
  - `item` integer, id|name
- `footage.info` (reads): Returns the Footage panel state: the open item, its name, the panel time (seconds, frame, timecode), the In and Out points, duration and frame rate; null when no footage is open. No parameters.
- `footage.setTime` (writes): Moves the Footage panel's time to `time` (source seconds) or `frame`, clamped to the footage. Returns the time in seconds; changes no composition.
  - `frame` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number, (s, source) | frame?
- `footage.setIn` (writes): Sets the Footage panel's In point for the open footage at `time` (source seconds) or `frame`, default the panel time; the range overlay and insert edits use.
  - `frame` integer, default: the panel's time; one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number, default: the panel's time; one of several alternative parameters
- `footage.setOut` (writes): Sets the Footage panel's Out point for the open footage at `time` (source seconds) or `frame`, default the panel time; the range overlay and insert edits use.
  - `frame` integer, default: the panel's time; one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number, default: the panel's time; one of several alternative parameters
- `footage.clearInOut` (writes): Clears the In and Out points set in the Footage panel for the open footage item. Changes no composition. No parameters.
- `footage.overlayEdit` (writes): Places footage `item` (its In–Out range from the Footage panel or `in`/`out` seconds) as a new layer in `comp` at `at` (default now), on top, overlapping what's there. Use footage.rippleInsertEdit to push later layers instead.
  - `at` number, comp s; default the current time
  - `comp` integer
  - `in` number, (s)
  - `item` integer
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `out` number, (s)
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `footage.rippleInsertEdit` (writes): Inserts footage `item`'s In–Out range (or `in`/`out` seconds) into `comp` at `at` (default now) and splits and pushes every later layer later by its length. Use footage.overlayEdit to overlap instead.
  - `at` number, comp s; default the current time
  - `comp` integer
  - `in` number, (s)
  - `item` integer
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `out` number, (s)
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `layer.nudge` (writes): The arrow keys in the Composition panel: move the selected (unlocked) layers by `x`, `y` comp pixels; After Effects nudges 1 pixel at the panel's magnification, 10 with Shift. Each call is one undo step.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `merge` string
  - `x` number
  - `y` number, comp pixels
- `layer.align` (writes): Aligns `layers` (default selected) by `edge` (left, hcenter, right, top, vcenter, bottom) to the composition (default) or to the selection's bounds, moving their positions. Use layer.distribute to space them evenly.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `edge` string, one of `left` | `hcenter` | `right` | `top` | `vcenter` | `bottom`
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `to` string, one of `composition` | `selection`, default composition
- `layer.distribute` (writes): Spaces three or more `layers` (default selected) evenly between the outermost two by `mode`: left, hcenter, right (horizontal) or top, vcenter, bottom (vertical) edges or centres. Use layer.align to line them up.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `edge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `mode` string, one of `left` | `hcenter` | `right` | `top` | `vcenter` | `bottom`, edges or centres
- `contentFill.set` (writes): Sets the Content-Aware Fill options used by layer.newContentAwareFill: `method` (object, surface, edgeBlend), `range` (workArea, entire), `alphaExpansion` (px), `lightingCorrection` (none, subtle, moderate, strong), `referenceLayer`, `referenceTime` (s).
  - `alphaExpansion` number, px
  - `lightingCorrection` string, one of `none` | `subtle` | `moderate` | `strong`
  - `method` string, object|surface|edgeBlend
  - `range` string, one of `workArea` | `entire`
  - `referenceLayer` integer or string, layer|null
  - `referenceTime` number, s
- `contentFill.generate` (writes): Generates a Content-Aware Fill layer for `layer` from its masks, using the Content-Aware Fill panel settings (parameters override them): fills the masked area from surrounding frames. Needs a mask on the layer.
  - `alphaExpansion` number, (px)
  - `layer` integer
  - `lightingCorrection` string, one of `none` | `subtle` | `moderate` | `strong`
  - `method` string, object|surface|edgeBlend
  - `outputDir` string
  - `range` string, one of `workArea` | `entire`
  - `referenceLayer` string
  - `referenceTime` number, s
  - `wait` boolean
- `storage.info` (reads): Returns the browser storage the web app uses: availability, backend, usage and quota, whether storage is persistent, stored files by kind and the disk cache statistics. {available: false} on desktop. No parameters.
- `storage.persist` (writes): Asks the browser to make the web app's storage persistent so it isn't evicted. Returns {requested, persisted}. No parameters.
- `storage.clear` (writes): Delete stored data: `diskCache` (cached frames), `media` (imported footage), `projects` (saved projects), `autoSaves`, or `all` of them (settings stay). Returns what was removed: `{cleared, entries, bytes}`.
  - `what` string, one of `diskCache` | `media` | `projects` | `autoSaves` | `all`
- `learn.list` (reads): Lists the built-in tutorials: id, title, summary, minutes and step titles. Start one with learn.start. No parameters.
- `learn.state` (reads): Returns the running tutorial's state: id, current step, step count, completed steps and the current step's title, text, target and accepted commands; null when none is running.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `learn.start` (writes): Start `req`; replies go to `inbox` (ending with [`WorkerReply::Done`]).
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `tutorial` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `learn.step` (writes): Moves through the running tutorial: `action` next, back, goto (`index`) or showMe (runs the step's commands for you). Fails when no tutorial is running.
  - `action` string, one of `next` | `back` | `showMe` | `goto`
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `learn.stop` (writes): Closes the running tutorial. Changes no project content. No parameters.
- `templates.list` (reads): Lists the project templates: id, name, description, category, built-in or user, size, frame rate, duration and controls; `thumbnails: true` adds a 256×144 thumbnail.
  - `thumbnails` boolean
- `templates.thumbnail` (reads): Returns a template's thumbnail (`id`): width, height and RGB pixels as hex.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `templates.create` (writes): Replaces the open project with an untitled copy of a project template (`id` from templates.list, or `path` to an .ectemplate) and opens its main comp; embedded footage is extracted beside `projectPath` or into `footageDir`.
  - `footageDir` string
  - `id` integer or string, an id; templates.list; one of several alternative parameters
  - `path` file, .ectemplate; one of several alternative parameters
  - `projectPath` string, save the new project there; embedded footage goes to `<stem> Footage/` next to it
- `templates.delete` (writes): Deletes a saved user template (`id`, `user/<file>`). Built-in templates cannot be deleted.
  - `id` string, user/<file>
- `playback.settings.get` (reads): Returns the preview settings for a preview `shortcut` (spacebar by default): frame rate, skip, resolution, range, loop, audio, and the planned start, end and step for the active comp.
  - `shortcut` string, one of `spacebar` | `shiftSpacebar` | `numpad0` | `shiftNumpad0` | `altNumpad0`, default: the one shown in the Preview panel
- `playback.settings.set` (reads): Changes the Preview panel settings of a shortcut (`shortcut`, or `current`): range, frame rate, resolution, loop, whether video, audio and overlays play, pre- and post-roll, frames skipped; `reset: true` restores the defaults.
  - `cacheBeforePlayback` boolean
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `current` string, shortcut shown in the panel
  - `customResolution` integer
  - `frameRate` json, fps|"auto"
  - `fullScreen` boolean
  - `includeAudio` boolean
  - `includeLayerControls` boolean
  - `includeOverlays` boolean
  - `includeVideo` boolean
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `loop` boolean
  - `moveTimeToPreviewTime` boolean
  - `playCachedFrames` boolean
  - `playFrom` string, one of `rangeStart` | `currentTime`
  - `postRoll` number, seconds
  - `preRoll` number, seconds
  - `range` string, one of `workArea` | `workAreaExtended` | `entireDuration` | `aroundCurrentTime`
  - `reset` boolean
  - `resolution` string, one of `auto` | `full` | `half` | `third` | `quarter` | `custom`
  - `shortcut` string
  - `skip` integer, frames skipped between previewed frames, 0 to 99
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `values` object

### Edit

- `edit.undo` (writes): Undoes the last step. A step the replica holds is undone on the replica too, and the project becomes what the replica holds then (any collaborator's edits that arrived since kept); see [`kdm_bridge`].
  - `scope` string, one of `person` | `agent`
- `edit.redo` (writes): Redoes the last undone step in the caller's scope (`scope` person or agent; an agent's redo never redoes the person's step). Returns the label of the redone step, or null when there is nothing to redo.
  - `scope` string, one of `person` | `agent`
- `edit.cut` (writes): Edit ▸ Cut while editing text.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `edit.copy` (reads): Edit ▸ Copy: selected properties copy their keyframes and values, selected keyframes go to the keyframe clipboard, else layers.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `edit.copyWithPropertyLinks` (reads): Copies the selected properties, or whole `layers`, so that pasting creates expressions linking each pasted property to its original (absolute comp references). Use for driving copies from one master.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `enabled` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `edit.copyWithRelativePropertyLinks` (reads): Like edit.copyWithPropertyLinks, but the pasted expressions use thisComp, so they link to same-named layers in whatever comp the copy is pasted into.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `edit.copyExpressionOnly` (reads): Copies only the expressions of the selected properties (not their values or keys) to the clipboard; edit.paste then applies them to matching properties. Fails if none of them has an expression. No parameters.
- `edit.paste` (writes): Edit ▸ Paste while editing text: the copied text with its formatting, or `text` (from the system clipboard) in the caret's style when it's something else.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `enabled` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `edit.pasteReversedKeyframes` (writes): Edit ▸ Paste Reversed Keyframes: the copied keys mirrored in time over their whole span (the last key first, incoming and outgoing eases swapped), pasted like Edit ▸ Paste (`keys.paste`: at the current time, into the selected or the same properties).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number
- `edit.clear` (writes): Deletes `layers`: the command that deletes layers. Without `layers` it deletes the selection (keyframes, effects, masks or shape items when selected, else the selected layers), or, while text is being edited, the character before the caret.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `edit.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates the selected layers (or `layers`); when effects or shape items are selected, duplicates those instead. Answers the new ids.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `edit.splitLayer` (writes): Splits `layers` (default selected) at the current time into two layers: the original ends there and a copy starts there (placed above or below per the preference). Layers the current time doesn't cross are skipped; returns the new layers.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `edit.liftWorkArea` (writes): Removes the work area's time span from `layers` (default selected) and leaves a gap: layers are split at the work area edges and the part inside is deleted, later parts don't move. Use edit.extractWorkArea to close the gap.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `edit.extractWorkArea` (writes): Removes the work area's time span from `layers` (default selected) and closes the gap: layers are split and later parts shift earlier. Use edit.liftWorkArea to remove it and leave a gap.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `edit.selectAll` (reads): Selects all layers of the active comp that can be selected (not locked; not shy while shy layers are hidden). While editing text, selects all the text; with a puppet pin selected, every pin of that kind. No parameters.
- `edit.deselectAll` (reads): Clears the selection of layers, properties, keyframes and mask vertices. Changes no content. No parameters.
- `edit.editOriginal` (writes): Opens the source file of the selected footage item or layer in its default application (emits an open-URL request). Returns {url}; changes nothing in the project. No parameters.
- `edit.pasteTextMatchFormatting` (writes): Edit ▸ Paste Text and Match Formatting: the clipboard's plain text in the style at the caret.
  - `text` string
- `edit.pasteTextFormattingOnly` (writes): Edit ▸ Paste Text Formatting Only: the copied text's character style (its first character) and paragraph settings on the selected text, or on the whole of the selected text layers.
  - `caret` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `created` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `select` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `app.commandPalette` (reads): Editor window only: opens Quick Apply to search commands and effects by name. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; agents use <prefix>_commands.
  - `query` string
- `app.keyboardShortcuts` (reads): Editor window only: opens the keyboard shortcut editor. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters

### Edit > Label

- `edit.label` (writes): Sets the label colour (`label`: Red, Yellow, Aqua, …) of the selected or given `layers`, or of the selected keyframes (`keys`).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `keys` string
  - `label` string, Red|Yellow|Aqua|…
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `target` string, layers
- `edit.selectLabelGroup` (reads): Selects every layer of the active comp whose label colour matches a selected layer's; with no layer selected, every project item whose label matches a selected item's. No parameters.

### Edit > Purge

- `edit.purgeUndo` (writes): Clears the whole undo history (Edit › Purge › Undo); earlier states can no longer be restored. Changes no content. No parameters.

### Composition

- `comp.new` (writes): Creates a composition (default 1920×1080, 29.97 fps, 10 s) and makes it active: set `name`, `width`, `height`, `frameRate`, `duration` (s), `background` and `renderer`. Returns its id; add layers to it afterwards.
  - `adaptiveSampleLimit` integer, 16–256
  - `anchor` integer
  - `duration` number, s
  - `frameRate` number
  - `height` number
  - `motionBlurSamples` integer
  - `name` string
  - `open` boolean
  - `pixelAspect` number
  - `preserveFrameRate` boolean
  - `preserveResolution` boolean
  - `renderer` string, one of `classic3D` | `advanced3D`
  - `shutterAngle` number
  - `shutterPhase` number
  - `startTime` number, (s) | startTimecode?
  - `startTimecode` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `width` number
- `comp.settings` (writes): Changes a composition's settings: `name`, `width`/`height` (with `anchor` 0–8 for where content stays), `frameRate`, `duration`, `startTime`, `background`, shutter angle and phase, motion blur samples, renderer. `comp` defaults to the active one.
  - `adaptiveSampleLimit` integer, 16–256
  - `anchor` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `background` json
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `duration` number
  - `frameRate` number
  - `height` number
  - `motionBlurSamples` integer
  - `name` string
  - `pixelAspect` number
  - `preserveFrameRate` boolean, nested or in the render queue it shows only its own frames
  - `preserveResolution` boolean, nested, it renders at full size
  - `renderer` string, one of `classic3D` | `advanced3D`
  - `shutterAngle` number
  - `shutterPhase` number
  - `startTime` number, (s) | startTimecode?
  - `startTimecode` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `width` number
- `comp.setPosterTime` (writes): Sets the composition's poster frame (its thumbnail in the project) to the current time. Changes no layers.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `comp.trimToWorkArea` (writes): Shortens the composition to its work area: time before the work area start is cut, layers shift earlier so their content keeps its place, and the duration becomes the work area length.
  - `comp` integer or string
- `renderQueue.add` (writes): Adds `comp` to the Render Queue with output `format` (h264, hevc, av1, prores, webm, png/jpeg/tiff/exr sequences, gif, wav, aiff), `output` path, `template`, `resolution` and `quality`. Start it with renderQueue.render.
  - `audio` string, one of `auto` | `on` | `off`
  - `audioBitrate` number
  - `audioChannels` number or string
  - `audioFormat` string
  - `bitrate` number, kbps
  - `channels` string, one of `rgb` | `rgba` | `alpha`
  - `color` string
  - `colorDepth` json
  - `comp` integer or string, id|name
  - `crop` boolean
  - `duration` number, s
  - `effects` json
  - `end` number, s
  - `fieldRender` json
  - `format` string, one of `h264` | `hevc` | `av1` | `prores` | `webm` | `png` | `jpeg` | `tiff` | `exr` | `gif` | `wav` | `aiff`
  - `frameBlending` json
  - `frameRate` json, fps|null
  - `guideLayers` json
  - `includeProjectLink` boolean
  - `item` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `keyframeInterval` integer
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `level` number
  - `log` string, one of `errorsOnly` | `plusSettings` | `plusPerFrameInfo`
  - `loop` boolean, values as in setRenderSettings / setOutputModule
  - `motionBlur` json
  - `opusApplication` string
  - `output` string, path|template
  - `profile` string
  - `proresProfile` string
  - `proxyUse` string
  - `pulldown` json
  - `quality` json, best|draft|1-100 (jpeg, webm); jpeg, webm
  - `rateControl` string
  - `resize` object
  - `resolution` number, full|half|third|quarter|scale
  - `sampleRate` integer
  - `skipExisting` boolean
  - `solo` json
  - `start` number, s
  - `storageOverflow` boolean
  - `template` string, Render Settings template
  - `timeSpan` string, one of `workArea` | `comp` | `custom`
  - `webmBitrate` boolean
  - `webmCodec` string
- `render.addOutputModule` (writes): Composition ▸ Add Output Module: another output module on a render item (the same frames are encoded once more).
  - `audio` json
  - `bitrate` number
  - `channels` string
  - `format` string
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); default: the last item; one of several alternative parameters
  - `item` integer, default: the last item; one of several alternative parameters
  - `output` string
  - `proresProfile` string
  - `quality` json
- `render.preRender` (writes): Composition ▸ Pre-render…: queue the comp with a lossless-with-alpha module whose post-render action imports the result and replaces the comp's uses.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `format` string
  - `output` string, path|template
- `render.saveCurrentPreview` (writes): Composition ▸ Save Current Preview…: render the work area of the comp straight to a movie file.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `path` file
  - `wait` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `comp.cropToRegionOfInterest` (writes): Resizes `comp` to the viewer's region of interest and shifts its layers so they keep their place. Needs a region of interest drawn in the viewer.
  - `comp` integer or string
- `comp.cropToLayerBounds` (writes): Resizes the composition to the visible bounds of `layers` (default selected) at the current time and shifts every layer so nothing moves on screen. Fails when the layers draw nothing.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `comp.flowchart` (reads): Editor window only: opens the Composition Flowchart panel. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; read nesting with project queries. No parameters.
- `comp.miniFlowchart` (reads): Editor window only: shows the mini-flowchart of nested compositions. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing. No parameters.
- `comp.openInGraphicsTemplates` (writes): Composition ▸ Open in Graphics Templates.
  - `comp` integer or string

### Layer > New

- `layer.newText` (writes): Adds a text layer with `text` (point text at `position`, or paragraph text in `box` [x, y, w, h]) and character options: `font`, `size`, `fill`, `stroke`, `tracking`, `leading`, `justify`. Edit it later with layer.setText. Returns the layer.
  - `allCaps` boolean
  - `applyFill` boolean
  - `applyStroke` boolean
  - `baseline` string
  - `baselineShift` number
  - `box` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `composer` string
  - `direction` string
  - `edit` boolean, start editing
  - `fauxBold` boolean
  - `fauxItalic` boolean
  - `fill` string or array, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1)
  - `font` string
  - `hScale` number
  - `hangingPunctuation` boolean
  - `indentFirst` number
  - `indentLeft` number
  - `indentRight` number
  - `justify` string
  - `kerning` string or number
  - `leading` number
  - `ligatures` boolean
  - `name` string, layer name; default the text
  - `position` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `size` number
  - `smallCaps` boolean
  - `spaceAfter` number
  - `spaceBefore` number
  - `stroke` string or array, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1)
  - `strokeOverFill` boolean
  - `strokeWidth` number
  - `style` string
  - `subscript` boolean
  - `superscript` boolean
  - `text` string
  - `tracking` number
  - `tsume` number
  - `vScale` number
  - `vertical` boolean
- `layer.newSolid` (writes): Adds a solid colour layer (`color` #hex or [r, g, b], default comp-sized `width`/`height`) at the top of the comp. Use for backgrounds or as a base for effects; use a shape layer for vector shapes. Returns the layer.
  - `color` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `height` number
  - `name` string
  - `pixelAspect` number
  - `width` number
- `layer.newNull` (writes): A new null at `at` (comp space) named `name`, made unique in the comp (expressions find layers by name). Returns (layer id, name).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `name` string
- `layer.newShape` (writes): Adds a new shape layer with one shape: `kind` rect, rounded, ellipse, polygon or star (none for an empty layer) of `size` [w, h] (default 300 × 300), centred at `position`. Paint: `fill` (default blue) or `fillGradient` (two or more colours, `fillAngle` in degrees, `fillType: radial` for a radial one), and `stroke` with `strokeWidth`; the Tools bar's paint is not used. Returns the layer.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `fill` string or array or boolean, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1), or false for none
  - `fillAngle` json, deg
  - `fillBlend` string, a blend mode name (normal, multiply, …)
  - `fillGradient` array
  - `fillOpacity` number, percent, 0 to 100
  - `fillType` string, one of `none` | `solid` | `linear` | `radial`
  - `kind` string, one of `rect` | `rounded` | `ellipse` | `star` | `polygon` | `none`
  - `name` string
  - `position` json[]
  - `size` array or number, pixels: [w, h], or one number for both
  - `stroke` string or array or boolean, a colour, "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0 to 1), or false for none
  - `strokeAngle` json
  - `strokeBlend` string, a blend mode name (normal, multiply, …)
  - `strokeGradient` json
  - `strokeOpacity` number, percent, 0 to 100
  - `strokeType` string, one of `none` | `solid` | `linear` | `radial`
  - `strokeWidth` number
- `layer.newAdjustment` (writes): Adds an adjustment layer the size of the comp: effects on it apply to every layer below it. Same options as layer.newSolid (`name`, `width`, `height`).
  - `name` string
- `layer.newLight` (writes): Adds a light layer: `kind` Parallel, Spot (default), Point, Ambient or Environment, with color, intensity, cone, falloff and shadow options. Lights affect 3D layers; Environment lights from an equirectangular image layer.
  - `castsShadows` boolean
  - `color` string
  - `coneAngle` number
  - `coneFeather` number
  - `falloff` number, None|Smooth|Inverse Square Clamped
  - `falloffDistance` number
  - `intensity` number
  - `kind` string, one of `Parallel` | `Spot` | `Point` | `Ambient` | `Environment`, default Spot; Environment lights and reflects from an equirectangular image layer: prop.set its lightOptions/source to that layer's id, or leave it empty for the comp's Environment Layer, see layer.environment
  - `name` string
  - `radius` number
  - `shadowDarkness` number
  - `shadowDiffusion` number
- `layer.newCamera` (writes): Adds a camera layer: `type` oneNode or twoNode (default, with a point of interest), lens `preset` (15–200mm) or `zoom`/`focalLength`/`angleOfView`, depth of field options, `position` and `poi` [x, y, z]. Only 3D layers see it.
  - `aperture` number
  - `blurLevel` number
  - `dof` boolean
  - `fStop` number
  - `focusDistance` number
  - `lockToZoom` boolean
  - `name` string
  - `preset` string, one of `15mm` | `20mm` | `24mm` | `28mm` | `35mm` | `50mm` | `80mm` | `135mm` | `200mm`, 15mm|20mm|24mm|28mm|35mm|50mm|80mm|135mm|200mm
  - `type` string, one of `oneNode` | `twoNode`, default twoNode
  - `zoom` number
- `layer.newContentAwareFill` (writes): Content-Aware Fill: renders a fill layer that removes the masked area of `layer` over the work area or the whole comp, with the options of contentFill.set (or given here); writes the frames to `outputDir`.
  - `alphaExpansion` number, (px)
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `lightingCorrection` string, one of `none` | `subtle` | `moderate` | `strong`
  - `method` string, object|surface|edgeBlend
  - `outputDir` string
  - `range` string, one of `workArea` | `entire`
  - `referenceLayer` string
  - `referenceTime` number, s
  - `wait` boolean

### Layer

- `layer.settings` (writes): Layer ▸ Layer Settings: cameras and lights open their own settings; solids (and adjustment layers, which are solids) edit their Solid Settings.
  - `affectAll` boolean, default true; false gives this layer its own copy of a solid other layers use
  - `color` string
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `height` number
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string
  - `pixelAspect` number
  - `width` number
- `layer.precompose` (writes): Moves `layers` (default selected) into a new composition `name` and replaces them with one layer of it (`mode: move`), or keeps a single layer's attributes outside (`mode: leave`); `adjustDuration` fits it to the layers, `open` opens it.
  - `adjustDuration` boolean
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `mode` string, one of `move` | `leave`
  - `name` string
  - `open` boolean
- `layer.environment` (writes): Makes footage, comp or solid `layers` (default selected) environment layers (`on`, default toggles): a 360° image that lights and reflects in Advanced 3D. Turns their 3D switch on; model and light layers are refused.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `on` boolean
- `path.groupShapes` (writes): Puts the selected shape items (in one group of a shape layer's contents) into a new group, so they share a transform. Fails when they are in different groups.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `items` json[], [uid]
  - `layer` integer
- `path.ungroupShapes` (writes): Dissolves the selected shape groups, moving their items into the parent group; a static group transform is baked into the items.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `items` json[], [group uid]
  - `layer` integer
- `layer.openSource` (writes): Opens a layer's source: a precomp layer's composition becomes the active comp (returns {comp}); footage opens in the Footage panel in the editor.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
- `layer.revealInFinder` (writes): Opens the folder holding `layer`'s source file in the system file browser. Returns {url}; fails when the source is not a file.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
- `layer.openLayer` (writes): Editor window only: opens `layer` in the Layer panel. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing.
  - `layer` integer
- `layer.autoTrace` (writes): Traces the edges of `layer` (its `channel`: alpha, red, green, blue or luminance) into masks, at the current frame or over the work area (`timeSpan`): `threshold`, `blur`, `tolerance`, `minimumArea`, `cornerRoundness`, `invert`; `applyToNewLayer` puts the masks on a new solid.
  - `applyToNewLayer` boolean
  - `blur` number, px, 1
  - `channel` string, one of `alpha` | `red` | `green` | `blue` | `luminance`
  - `cornerRoundness` number, %, 50
  - `invert` boolean
  - `layer` integer
  - `minimumArea` number, px, 10
  - `threshold` number, %, 50
  - `timeSpan` string, one of `currentFrame` | `workArea`
  - `tolerance` number, px, 1
- `layer.sceneEditDetection` (writes): Finds the cuts in a video layer and marks them (`mode` markers), splits the layer at them (split) or splits and precomposes the parts (splitPrecompose); `threshold` 0…1 (default 0.25).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `mode` string, one of `markers` | `split` | `splitPrecompose`
  - `threshold` number, 0…1, 0.25
  - `wait` boolean

### Layer > Arrange

- `layer.arrange` (writes): Changes the stacking order of `layers` (default selected): `to` front, forward, backward or back, or an exact `index` (1-based), or `above` another layer. Upper layers draw over lower ones; locked layers are refused.
  - `above` integer or string, layer
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `to` string, one of `front` | `forward` | `backward` | `back`

### Layer > Mask

- `layer.addMask` (writes): Adds a mask to `layer`: `shape` rect, ellipse, rounded, polygon or star; `rect` [x, y, w, h] in layer pixels (default the whole layer); `mode` add, subtract and so on. Use mask commands to edit its path, feather and opacity.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `mode` string
  - `rect` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `shape` string, one of `rect` | `ellipse` | `rounded` | `polygon` | `star`
- `layer.mask.hideLocked` (writes): Hides or shows locked masks in the viewer (`value`, default toggles). Display only; masks still apply.
  - `value` boolean
- `layer.mask.shape` (writes): Sets a mask's path to a `shape` rect or ellipse filling `rect` [x, y, w, h] in layer pixels, for `mask` (default selected) on `layer`.
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `rect` number[]
  - `shape` string, one of `rect` | `ellipse`
- `layer.mask.reset` (writes): Resets the target masks to a full-layer rectangle with no feather, 100% opacity, no expansion, mode Add and not inverted, removing their keyframes and expressions.
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
- `layer.mask.remove` (writes): Deletes `mask` from `layer`; without `mask`, the selected masks, else the first one. layer.mask.removeAll deletes them all.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `mask` integer
- `layer.mask.removeAll` (writes): Deletes every mask on `layers` (default selected).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.mask.invert` (writes): Inverts or un-inverts the target masks (`value`, default toggles): an inverted mask keeps the outside instead of the inside.
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `value` boolean
- `layer.mask.lock` (writes): Locks or unlocks `mask` on `layer` (`value`, default toggles); locked masks can't be selected or edited in the viewer.
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
  - `value` boolean
- `layer.mask.unlockAll` (writes): Unlocks every mask on `layers` (default selected).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.mask.lockOthers` (writes): Locks every mask on the layer except the target ones (`mask`, default selected), so only those can be edited.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `mask` integer

### Layer > Transform

- `layer.transform` (writes): Applies a transform shortcut to `layers` at the current time: `op` reset (defaults), center (centre in the comp), fit, fitWidth, fitHeight (scale to the comp), flipH or flipV.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `op` string, one of `reset` | `center` | `fit` | `fitWidth` | `fitHeight` | `flipH` | `flipV`
- `layer.autoOrient` (writes): Layer ▸ Transform ▸ Auto-Orient: off | alongPath | towardsCamera (3D layers) | towardsPointOfInterest (cameras and spot/parallel lights).
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `mode` string, one of `off` | `alongPath` | `towardsCamera` | `towardsPointOfInterest`
- `layer.centerAnchor` (writes): Moves the anchor point of `layers` (default selected) to the centre of their visible content and compensates position, so nothing moves on screen; rotation and scale then pivot around the content's centre.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]

### Layer > Layer Styles

- `layer.style.convertToEditable` (writes): Converts the Photoshop layer styles of layers imported from PSD files into editable styles. Layers made here have none to convert.
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.style.showAll` (writes): Show All: every style is added (new ones switched off) so they can be revealed and edited.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.style.removeAll` (writes): Deletes every layer style from `layers` (default selected). Returns how many layers had styles.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.style.dropShadow` (writes): Adds a Drop Shadow layer style to `layers` (default selected): a shadow offset behind their visible pixels, using the comp's global light angle by default. Same as layer.style.add with dropShadow.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object, size, color, opacity, …; names as the answer lists them
- `layer.style.innerShadow` (writes): Adds an Inner Shadow layer style to `layers` (default selected): a shadow cast inside their visible edges, as if cut out.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object, size, color, opacity, …; names as the answer lists them
- `layer.style.outerGlow` (writes): Adds an Outer Glow layer style to `layers` (default selected): a glow around the outside of their visible pixels.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object, size, color, opacity, …; names as the answer lists them
- `layer.style.innerGlow` (writes): Adds an Inner Glow layer style to `layers` (default selected): a glow along the inside edges of their visible pixels.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object, size, color, opacity, …; names as the answer lists them
- `layer.style.bevelEmboss` (writes): Adds a Bevel and Emboss layer style to `layers` (default selected), giving them raised edges with highlight and shadow. Same as layer.style.add with bevelEmboss.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object, size, color, opacity, …; names as the answer lists them
- `layer.style.satin` (writes): Adds a Satin layer style to `layers` (default selected): interior shading that gives a glossy, silky look.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object, size, color, opacity, …; names as the answer lists them
- `layer.style.colorOverlay` (writes): Adds a Color Overlay layer style to `layers` (default selected), filling their visible pixels with one colour. Same as layer.style.add with colorOverlay.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object, size, color, opacity, …; names as the answer lists them
- `layer.style.gradientOverlay` (writes): Adds a Gradient Overlay layer style to `layers` (default selected), filling their visible pixels with a gradient. Same as layer.style.add with gradientOverlay.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object, size, color, opacity, …; names as the answer lists them
- `layer.style.stroke` (writes): Adds a Stroke layer style to `layers` (default selected): an outline around their visible pixels. For brush strokes on a layer use paint.stroke instead.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `params` object, size, color, opacity, …; names as the answer lists them
- `layer.style.options` (writes): Editor window only: opens the Layer Style options dialog. Headless sessions accept it and change nothing; set style properties with prop.set.
  - `layer` integer
  - `style` string, blendingOptions|dropShadow|…

### Layer > Camera

- `layer.cameraSettings` (writes): Changes a camera layer: `name`, `type` (one- or two-node), `preset` or `zoom`/`focalLength`/`angleOfView`, depth of field (`dof`, `focusDistance`, `aperture`/`fStop`, `blurLevel`), `position` and point of interest `poi`, keyed at the current time.
  - `angleOfView` number
  - `aperture` number
  - `blurLevel` number
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `dof` boolean
  - `fStop` number
  - `focalLength` number
  - `focusDistance` number
  - `layer` integer
  - `name` string
  - `poi` number[], [x, y, z]
  - `position` number[], [x, y, z]
  - `preset` string
  - `type` string
  - `zoom` number
- `camera.fromView` (writes): Layer ▸ Camera ▸ Create Camera from 3D View: a two-node camera matching the current 3D view.
  - `comp` integer or string
- `camera.stereoRig` (writes): Builds a stereo 3D rig in `comp`: a master camera (the active one or new), left and right eye cameras and comps, a Stereo 3D Controls layer and a 3D Glasses output. `configuration`, `sceneDepth` (% of width) and `convergence` set the rig.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `configuration` string, one of `stereoPair` | `centerRight` | `centerLeft`
  - `convergence` boolean
  - `convergenceOf` string, one of `poi` | `zoom`
  - `sceneDepth` number, % of comp width, default 3
  - `view3d` integer, 3D Glasses view index (default 5 Balanced Colored Red Blue); default 5 Balanced Colored Red Blue
  - `zOffset` number
- `camera.orbitNull` (writes): Create Orbit Null: a 3D null at the camera's point of interest becomes the camera's parent, so rotating the null orbits the camera around what it looks at.
  - `camera` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `layer` integer or string, camera (default selected/active); default selected/active
- `camera.fromModel` (writes): Creates a camera layer for every camera inside the 3D model layers (`layers`, default selected) of `comp`, matching their position, orientation and zoom.
  - `comp` integer
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, 3D model layers (default selected); default selected
- `camera.linkFocusToPoi` (writes): Adds an expression on the camera's Focus Distance equal to the distance from its position to its point of interest, so focus follows the target.
  - `camera` integer
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `camera.linkFocusToLayer` (writes): Adds an expression on the camera's Focus Distance that tracks the distance to `layer`, so focus follows it over time; use camera.setFocusToLayer for a one-time value.
  - `camera` integer
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `layer` integer
- `camera.setFocusToLayer` (writes): Sets the camera's Focus Distance, keyed at the current time, to `layer`'s current distance from it. Fails if the layer is behind the camera; camera.linkFocusToLayer keeps following it.
  - `camera` integer
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `layer` integer

### View > Switch 3D View

- `view.3d.activeCamera` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to the Active Camera (what renders). View state only; the project is unchanged.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.default` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to the Default camera view. View state only.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.front` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to Front (orthographic). View state only.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.left` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to Left (orthographic). View state only.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.top` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to Top (orthographic). View state only.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.back` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to Back (orthographic). View state only.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.right` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to Right (orthographic). View state only.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.bottom` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to Bottom (orthographic). View state only.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.custom1` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to Custom View 1 (a perspective working view). View state only.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.custom2` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to Custom View 2. View state only.
  - `comp` integer
- `view.3d.custom3` (reads): Switches the comp viewer's 3D view to Custom View 3. View state only.
  - `comp` integer

### View

- `view.3d.last` (reads): Switches the comp viewer back to the previously used 3D view. View state only.
  - `comp` integer or string
- `view.lookAtSelected` (writes): Frames the current 3D view on the given `layers` (or the selection); with the Active Camera view this moves the camera layer (undoable). Use view.lookAtAll to fit everything.
  - `comp` integer
  - `layers` integer[]
- `view.lookAtAll` (writes): Frames the current 3D view so every active non-camera, non-light layer is visible; with the Active Camera view this moves the camera layer (undoable). Use view.lookAtSelected for a subset.
  - `comp` integer
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `view.reset3DView` (writes): Resets the current 3D view. For a custom or orthographic view it drops the stored view camera; for Active Camera it moves the camera layer back to default framing of the comp centre (undoable; fails without a camera layer).
  - `comp` integer or string
- `time.set` (reads): Moves the current time (CTI) of the active comp to `time` (seconds), `frame` or `timecode`. Commands that act at the current time, such as keying and previews, use it.
  - `frame` integer, one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number, (s) | frame? | timecode?
  - `timecode` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `view.addGuide` (writes): Adds a guide to `comp`: `orientation` vertical (default) or horizontal at `position` in comp pixels (default the centre). Guides are saved with the comp but don't render.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `orientation` string, one of `vertical` | `horizontal`
  - `position` number, comp px
- `view.clearGuides` (writes): Removes every guide from `comp`.
  - `comp` integer or string
- `view.importGuides` (writes): Reads a guides JSON file written by view.exportGuides at `path` and appends its guides to the comp (undoable). Existing guides stay. Returns {imported: count}.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `path` file
- `view.exportGuides` (reads): Writes the comp's ruler guides, with its width and height, to a JSON file at `path`; returns {path, guides: count}. Load them into another comp with view.importGuides.
  - `path` file
- `view.snapping` (reads): Sets (`value`) or toggles layer snapping in the viewer. Session state only; the document is unchanged. Returns the new value.
  - `value` boolean
- `view.displayColorManagement` (reads): View ▸ Use Display Color Management (toggle, or `value`).
  - `value` boolean
- `view.splitLockedViewer` (reads): View ▸ Split with New Locked Viewer: lock a second viewer to the comp (default the active one) and its current 3D view (or `view`).
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `view` string, 3D view id
- `view.zoomIn` (reads): Frontend-only: zooms the viewer in one step. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing. No parameters.
- `view.zoomOut` (reads): Frontend-only: zooms the viewer out one step. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing. No parameters.
- `view.rulers` (reads): Frontend-only: toggles the viewer's rulers. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing.
  - `value` string
- `view.guides` (reads): Frontend-only: toggles the display of ruler guides in the viewer. Guides themselves are edited with view.moveGuide and view.removeGuide.
  - `value` string
- `view.snapToGuides` (reads): Frontend-only: toggles snapping layer drags to ruler guides. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing.
  - `value` string
- `view.lockGuides` (reads): Frontend-only: toggles whether guides can be dragged in the viewer. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing.
  - `value` string
- `view.grid` (reads): Frontend-only: toggles the viewer's grid overlay. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing.
  - `value` string
- `view.snapToGrid` (reads): Frontend-only: toggles snapping layer drags to the viewer grid. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing; use view.snapping for the session's snapping flag.
  - `redo` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `steps` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `value` string
- `view.options` (reads): Frontend-only: opens the View Options dialog. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing. No parameters.
- `view.layerControls` (reads): Frontend-only: toggles layer handles, masks and motion paths in the viewer. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing.
  - `value` string
- `view.fullScreen` (reads): Frontend-only: asks the editor to show the viewer full screen. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing. No parameters.
- `view.newViewer` (reads): Frontend-only: opens another viewer panel. Headless sessions accept it and do nothing. No parameters.

### Layer > Material

- `material.revealSource` (writes): Selects the 3D model file a model `layer`'s material comes from in the project panel. Returns {item}; fails when the material is the layer's own.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
- `material.reset` (writes): Resets the material of `layers` (default selected) to its defaults (for model layers, the model file's own materials). Returns the layers.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `material.duplicateAssign` (writes): Duplicate and Assign Material: the first layer's Material Options are copied onto the other selected layers of the same kind.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[], first = source

### Layer > Light

- `light.fromModel` (writes): Creates a light layer for every light inside the 3D model layers (`layers`, default selected) of `comp`, matching their type, colour, intensity and placement.
  - `comp` integer
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, 3D model layers (default selected); default selected
- `light.controlWithCamera` (writes): Control Light with Camera: the light rides on the camera (parented at the camera's eye, shining where it looks). Again (or `on: false`) releases it where it is.
  - `camera` integer, default active
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` array, lights (default selected); default selected
  - `on` boolean, default toggle
- `light.environmentBackground` (writes): Create Environment Light Background Layer: a layer showing the environment light's image as the scene's backdrop (an equirectangular sky drawn through the camera).
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `layer` integer or string, environment light (default selected / first); default selected / first
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `on` boolean, read by the command beside its listed parameters

### Animation > Animate Text

- `text.animatorFontAxes` (writes): Animation ▸ Animate Text ▸ Variable Font Axes: the axes of the layer's font, or (with `axis`) a new animator — or a property on `animator` — that offsets that axis (user units, weighted by the selectors, added to the axis default).
  - `animator` integer, uid|index
  - `axis` string, tag|name (omit to list the font's axes); omit to list the font's axes
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer

### Layer > Time

- `layer.timeStretch` (writes): Changes the playback speed of `layers` by `percent` (200 = half speed) or to a new `duration` in seconds, keeping the In point, current time or Out point fixed (`hold` in, current, out); `op: reverse` reverses.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `duration` number, s; one of several alternative parameters
  - `hold` string, one of `in` | `current` | `out`
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `op` string, reverse
  - `percent` number, s; one of several alternative parameters
  - `tracker` integer or string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `layer.timeReverse` (writes): Plays footage or comp `layers` (default selected) backwards over the same In and Out points (time stretch −100%). Run again to restore.
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.enableTimeRemap` (writes): Turns time remapping on or off (`value`, default toggles) for footage or comp `layers`: adds a Time Remap property keyed at the layer's start and end, which you then key to speed up, slow down, reverse or hold.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `value` boolean
- `layer.freezeFrame` (writes): Freezes footage or comp `layers` (default selected) on the frame they show at the current time: adds time remapping held at that frame for the whole layer.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.freezeOnLastFrame` (writes): Holds footage or comp `layers` on their last source frame from the current time on: adds time remapping that plays normally until now, then freezes.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.alignVideoToData` (writes): Lines a video layer up in time with a data footage item (`data`, with `key` its time field): the video's start `videoStart` (default the file's creation time) is matched against the data's samples, whose first sample sits at `dataStart` (comp seconds, default 0), and the layer is moved so both share one clock.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `data` string, data footage id|name
  - `dataStart` number, comp s of the first sample, 0
  - `key` string, time field
  - `layer` integer
  - `videoStart` string, ISO date-time | hh:mm:ss | timecode | seconds (default: file creation time); default: file creation time

### Animation

- `prop.setExpression` (writes): `{layer?, path|prop, ...}` for one property, or (Animation > Add Expression) no `path`/`prop` for the properties selected in the timeline, all in one undo step.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `enabled` boolean
  - `expression` string
  - `layer` integer
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
  - `time` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `keys.toggleHold` (writes): Toggles Hold interpolation on the selected keyframes' outgoing side: the value jumps at the next key instead of moving; toggling off restores Bezier (eased keys) or Linear. No parameters.
- `keys.interpolation` (writes): Sets the selected keyframes' interpolation: `interpolation` (linear, bezier, continuousBezier, autoBezier, hold) or `in`/`out` per side, `spatial` for paths, and roving. Changes how values move between keys, not the key values.
  - `autoBezier` boolean
  - `continuous` boolean
  - `interpolation` string, one of `linear` | `bezier` | `continuousBezier` | `autoBezier` | `hold`
  - `roving` boolean
  - `spatial` string, one of `linear` | `bezier` | `continuousBezier` | `autoBezier`
- `keys.velocity` (writes): Sets the speed and influence of the selected keyframes: `inSpeed`, `inInfluence` %, `outSpeed`, `outInfluence` % (numbers, or arrays per dimension), `continuous` to tie both sides. Use for custom eases; keys.easyEase for the standard one.
  - `continuous` boolean
  - `inInfluence` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `inSpeed` number or array, a number, or one per dimension
  - `merge` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `outInfluence` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `outSpeed` number or array, a number, or one per dimension
- `prop.separateDimensions` (writes): Splits a layer's Position into separate X, Y (and Z) properties so each can be keyed on its own (`value` true), or joins them back (false); default toggles. Keyframes are split or merged accordingly.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `value` boolean
- `anim.savePreset` (writes): Saves the selected properties (with their keyframes, relative to the earliest key) and selected effects as an .ecpreset file at `path` (`name` optional). Needs a selection; the comp is unchanged.
  - `name` string
  - `path` file, .ecpreset
- `anim.applyPreset` (writes): Applies an animation preset saved by anim.savePreset (`path` to an .ecpreset, or the preset JSON inline as `preset`) to `layers` (default selected): adds its effects and keyed properties from the current time, and records it as recent.
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `path` file, one of several alternative parameters
  - `preset` string, one of several alternative parameters
- `anim.addKeyframe` (writes): Keys every selected property at the current time (CTI): turns on animation for an unkeyed property, else adds a key holding its current value. Needs selected properties; use prop.addKey to key one property by path. No parameters.
- `text.removeAllAnimators` (writes): Deletes every text animator from text `layers` (default selected), returning the text to its unanimated look.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `anim.browsePresets` (writes): Editor window only: opens the animation preset browser. Headless sessions (agents) accept it and change nothing; use anim.applyPreset instead. No parameters.
- `track.motion` (writes): Adds a transform motion tracker (one track point) to the footage `layer` (default selected) and makes it current; place its point with track.setPoint, then track.analyze and track.apply to a target layer.
  - `layer` integer
- `track.stabilize` (writes): Adds a stabilize tracker to the footage `layer` (default selected): after analysis, applying it moves the layer itself to cancel camera shake.
  - `layer` integer
- `track.property` (writes): Track this Property: track another layer and drive the selected property's layer.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `source` integer or string, layer
- `track.mask` (writes): Tracks a mask (`mask`, default selected) on `layer` so its path follows the footage: `method` position, positionScale, positionScaleRotation, …Skew, perspective, faceOutline or faceDetailed; `direction`, `start`/`end`; `wait` blocks.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `direction` string, one of `forward` | `backward` | `frameForward` | `frameBackward`
  - `end` number, s
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer, uid|index|name
  - `method` string, one of `position` | `positionScale` | `positionScaleRotation` | `positionScaleRotationSkew` | `perspective` | `faceOutline` | `faceDetailed`
  - `start` number, s
  - `wait` boolean, block until done
- `track.warpStabilizer` (writes): Animation ▸ Warp Stabilizer VFX / the Tracker panel button: apply the effect to the selected layer and start analysing it.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `wait` boolean
- `track.camera` (writes): Animation ▸ Track Camera / the Tracker panel button: apply the 3D Camera Tracker to the layer (reusing one it already has), set the given options and start the analysis.
  - `angleOfView` number, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `aov` number, degrees
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `detailed` boolean
  - `layer` integer
  - `lensDistortion` boolean, solve k1/k2
  - `shotType` string, one of `fixed` | `variable` | `specify`
  - `solveMethod` string, one of `auto` | `typical` | `flat` | `tripod`
  - `undistort` boolean, render undistorted
  - `wait` boolean
- `templateProps.addProperty` (writes): Add Property to Graphics Templates: `{layer, path|prop}` or the selected properties.
  - `as` string, font (Source Text font family/style/size) | scale (uniform Scale); Source Text font family/style/size; uniform Scale
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `control` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `group` integer, control id
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `layer` integer
  - `mirror` boolean, a property already present is added as a mirror; default true
  - `name` string
  - `path` string, uid (default: the selected properties); default: the selected properties; one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` integer, uid (default: the selected properties); default: the selected properties; one of several alternative parameters
  - `text` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters

### Animation > Keyframe Assistant

- `prop.convertExpressionToKeyframes` (writes): Bakes a property's expression into a keyframe on every frame of the layer and disables the expression, so the result no longer depends on it. For `layer` plus `path`/`prop`.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `path` string, one of several alternative parameters
  - `prop` json, one of several alternative parameters
- `keys.easyEase` (writes): Applies Easy Ease to the selected keyframes: Bezier interpolation with 33% influence and zero speed on both sides (`which` in or out for one side), so motion slows into and out of each key.
  - `which` string, one of `both` | `in` | `out`
- `keys.easyEaseIn` (writes): Eases only the incoming side of the selected keyframes (Bezier, zero speed, 33% influence), so motion slows into each key; the outgoing side is unchanged.
  - `which` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `keys.easyEaseOut` (writes): Eases only the outgoing side of the selected keyframes (Bezier, zero speed, 33% influence), so motion starts slowly from each key; the incoming side is unchanged.
  - `which` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
- `keys.timeReverse` (writes): Keyframe Assistant ▸ Time-Reverse Keyframes: mirror the selected keys of each property. No parameters.
- `layer.sequence` (writes): Places two or more `layers` (in selection order) one after another in time; `overlap` with `duration` seconds overlaps them, `transition` dissolveFront or crossDissolve adds opacity fades.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `duration` number, s
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[], in order
  - `overlap` boolean
  - `transition` string, one of `off` | `dissolveFront` | `crossDissolve`
- `keys.exponentialScale` (writes): Replaces the motion between two selected Scale keyframes with exponential scaling (keys every frame), so a zoom looks constant-speed. Needs two Scale keys selected on one layer. No parameters.
- `keys.audioToKeyframes` (writes): Animation ▸ Keyframe Assistant ▸ Convert Audio to Keyframes: an "Audio Amplitude" null with Left Channel, Right Channel and Both Channels sliders keyed on every frame of the work area with the amplitude of the comp's audible layers. One undo step.
  - `comp` integer or string
- `keys.rpfCameraImport` (writes): Animation ▸ Keyframe Assistant ▸ RPF Camera Import: a camera layer keyed from camera data. RPF/RLA files carry their camera in an undocumented block, so Kition Motion reads the same data from JSON or CSV exports (see `docs/preferences.md` ▸ RPF Camera Import). One undo step.
  - `comp` integer or string
  - `path` file, .json|.csv camera data

### Layer > Markers

- `layer.updateMarkersFromSource` (writes): Layer ▸ Markers ▸ Update Markers From Source: copy a precomp's composition markers onto the layer (layer time is the nested comp's time), skipping ones already there.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
- `layer.addMarker` (writes): Adds a marker with `comment` at `time` (comp seconds, default now) to `layers` (default selected), replacing a marker at that time; layers with locked markers are skipped. Returns `time` and `markers`: each added marker's `layer`, `index` (as markers.list shows it) and `time`.
  - `comment` string
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `time` number
- `layer.markersLock` (writes): Locks or unlocks the markers of `layers` (`value`, default toggles): locked markers can't be added, moved or deleted. Returns the new state.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]
  - `value` boolean
- `layer.deleteAllMarkers` (writes): Deletes every marker on `layers` (default selected); layers whose markers are locked are skipped.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layers` integer[]

### Layer > Mask and Shape Path

- `mask.setClosed` (writes): Closes (default) or opens (`closed: false`) `mask`'s path on `layer`; an open mask path doesn't cut out the layer but still works for strokes and effects.
  - `closed` boolean
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
- `path.rotoBezier` (writes): Turns RotoBezier on or off for `mask` (or the selected masks): `value`, default toggles. With it on, tangents are computed automatically from the vertices for smooth curves.
  - `comp` integer, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `layer` integer
  - `layers` array, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `mask` integer
  - `path` string, read by the command beside its listed parameters
  - `value` boolean
- `path.convertToBezier` (writes): Turns RotoBezier masks back into ordinary Bezier masks with editable tangents (for `mask` or the selected ones on `layer`). The shape stays the same.
  - `layer` integer
  - `mask` integer
